mares.name: CIRCIOS
mares.physical: It seems she is not very big but a good looking filly (quite Kingman) with quality and reasonably straightforward physically.

plans2027.raceRecord: Placed twice before winning a 7f fillies’ novice at 1/8 in July. Retired OR79.
plans2027.pedigree: This is a wonderful family. Could It Be Love is a big girl. Adelaide River (Australia) is a big horse, talented. Sold to Aus after placing in the Irish Derby and did fine, now back and lost his way but he is 1m2f to 1m4f. Her full-sister Everlasting was a Listed-winning miler and has a Frankel filly foal. She stays 10f but best over a mile. She’s a half-sister to a very good horse by Australia, which is why Frankel was a good place to start with her.
plans2027.analysis: Kingman and War Front can both pass on a little bit of temperament so I am inclined to tread carefully without knowing what she is like. Kingman can get all shapes and sizes so I’m not going to assume she’s big. Frankel still makes as much sense, but you’d like to see the foal. If you wanted to send her to America, where the best of her pedigree is from, Uncle Mo, I mentioned looking at Nyquist last year and I still like him for her. It would be 3x3 to Uncle Mo’s dam Playa Maya and he was a Champion 2YO and Kentucky Derby winner who has continued to do well at stud. However, Not This Time is also on our list and he is an excellent option. He is a top-class sire and has nicked very well with War Front mares, he has 3 SWs from 14 foals for 21% SWs to foals and she is out of a War Front mare. NTT hasn’t had many runners out of European-bred mares, but your own Shareholder is out of a mare by Invincible Spirit, which is a plus as well. It’s worth noting that Storm Cat and Green Desert are both spicy sire lines, as War Front can also be too, so if she is particularly hot then I would think twice if the temperaments will work. If you want to keep her in Europe, she was on the list of mares that would suit Night of Thunder. She is from a classy family of milers and a winner herself. From small samples, the cross is disappointing at the moment, though Bow Echo is by Night of Thunder out of an Invincible Spirit mare so it can work. He too is from a family with a top-class stallion on the page.

plans2027.title: CIRCIOS 2022 by Kingman ex Could It Be Love (War Front)
plans2027.raceRecord: 4yo bay mare. Won one race and second twice from 4 starts, all over seven furlongs (and all at three). She is in foal for the first time to Frankel.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the third foal out of Could It Be Love (War Front) who was placed 6 times at Stakes level including finishing second in the G1 Irish 1000 Guineas and is already the dam of two stakes winners. G3W ADELAIDE RIVER (Australia) was also second in the G1 Irish Derby and G1 Grand Prix De Paris in 2025. Her full sister EVERLASTING is a stakes winner and was placed at Group level – she also has a Frankel filly foal. Could It Be Love is also a sister to dual G1W and Champion Sire UNCLE MO. Another unraced sister Cleopatra’s Gift is the dam of lightly raced 2026 G3 Desmond Stakes placed Needle Match (Night Of Thunder) who might well win a Group race.

She has a Gun Runner 2yo filly and filly foal and this feels like an active young family in which the mares have been well covered recently and which could well keep improving.

Kingman made a slow start as BMS but has now had 8 SWs in total including 2026 2yo G3W MOONRISE (by Churchill), which brings his strike rate up to a very solid 3.9% SW/ (from 5 crops of runners). His 8 different SWs and 6 further stakes placed horses are all by different stallions so no obvious nicks, though interestingly two of his stakes winners are closely inbred to Rafha being by Kodiac and his son Ardad. Two are from the Galileo line being by Churchill and Sand Gzaelle but that is likely coincidence.
plans2027.analysis:
FRANKEL — She could easily go back to FRANKEL and although there are no new stakes winners bred on this cross, Kingman is now the broodmare sire of 2026 2yo G3W MOONRISE by Churchill who is also by Galileo. The family has also already worked with Galileo, having produced ADELAIDE RIVER by Australia and he is still in a league of his own on overall stakes winners to runners statistics.

SEA THE STARS — If you wanted to wait and see what her Frankel foal looks like, I think SEA THE STARS could be a really good option. I normally try to avoid inbreedings but this combination works really well [particularly the other way round ie Kingman / Sea The Stars], possibly because it is often a good physical match. He will be 20 next year and still fine to use but won't be around forever. She was a seven furlong filly from a family which can stay further which suits well and it seems a good idea to use him with a mare like her as he is not always easy to use. He is also a brother to Galileo by Cape Cross, damsire of Australia who produced ADELAIDE RIVER.

mares.name: CRIMSON ADVOCATE
mares.physical: She was a top class 2yo sprinter who trained on to stay the mile well at four and is very well bred - she is an exciting prospect and deserves the best. She sounds like a good looking filly with quality and enough bone but needs a correct stallion with good knees.

plans2027.raceRecord: Third on debut over 4.5f on dirt, she won a 5f Stakes on turf at Gulfstream Park and came over and won the Gr.2 Queen Mary, all for George Weaver. She had a break and returned in the Gr.1 Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint and was a respectable 6th (5f, firm). She had another break and returned with a 5f Stakes win on turf in May before Ascot. Switching to the Gosdens, she was down the field in the Gr.1 King’s Stand. She was second, beaten a nose, on return in the Listed Snowdrop Stakes to Soprano after a long layoff and won the Listed Conqueror Stakes (good) at Goodwood, both over 1m. Sticking to 1m, she took a good renewal of the Gr.2 Duke of Cambridge Stakes and was third in the Gr.1 Falmouth Stakes, her first try at that level since sprinting. She was a very fast and precocious 2yo and has developed into a genuine Gr.1 miler. Her last run, staying-on sixth to Fallen Angel in the Rothschild, was below par. Strong traveller, lovely mover and not short of speed, though she finishes like she would probably stay 1m2f, hits the line strong when she gets rolling.
plans2027.pedigree: Her pedigree has improved a lot since this time last year, her Gr.1-producing sister sold for $1.2m last November and produced the Gr.1 Breeders’ Cup juvenile Turf Sprint winner Cy Fair by Not This Time. Crimson is by the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile and Kentucky Derby winner Nyquist and out of a sprinter, so it’s no surprise she was out early but still progressed over a little further at three and four. Nyquist is siring offspring similar to himself, capable of showing up well at two and progressing over 8f-10f at 3+. Her dam was out nice and early, winning a 6f dirt maiden for fillies on her third start in July, the first of a run of four, including three Listed level Stakes: 5fT, 6fAW and 7fD. She didn’t win again but was multiple Stakes-placed, including the Gr.3 Azalea Stakes over 6fD. She was quick. She tried a mile once and didn’t get it and her better efforts were over 6f rather than 7f which stretched her.
plans2027.analysis: Crimson Advocate is very much in the mould of her pedigree, which is excellent. A lot of her family have clicked with sirelines that are close to redundant, bar the Gr.2 winner Lord Miles by Curlin and the Champion Caledonia Road, by Quality Road. Cy Fair is out of her sister by Arch, and by top sire Not This Time. I see no reason to complicate things and she looks made for him. The resulting foal would have as good a chance as any of getting a mile. In Europe, there is nothing strong pedigree-wise to go on but we know she boasts the ideal race record to produce a champion, winning a Royal Ascot 2yo race and then again two years later over a mile. We went to Frankel this year given her class and diversity. She was also on the suitable list for Night of Thunder as she is a top-class Gr.1 miler and she was precocious too and she is very worthy of him. Everything about both of those matings excites me so really it comes down to where you want to base her.

plans2027.title: CRIMSON ADVOCATE 2021 by Nyquist ex Citizen Advocate (Proud Citizen)
plans2027.raceRecord: 5yo mare and the winner of 5 races from 11 starts. She ran four times at two and won two races including the G2 Queen Mary Stakes over 5 furlongs at Royal Ascot. She came to England to be trained and only ran twice as a 3yo but won two races at four this year including the G2 Duke Of Cambridge Stakes over a mile at Royal Ascot. She also finished third in the G1 Falmouth Stakes. She is in foal to Frankel for the first time.
plans2027.pedigree:
Crimson Advocate is the 5th foal and first black type filly out of multiple 2yo stakes winner CITIZEN ADVOCATE (Proud Citizen). Citizen Advocate’s first foal Remarqued is now the dam of 2025 G1 Breeders Cup Turf Juvenile sprint winner CY FAIR (by NOT THIS TIME) who has trained on to win two G3s over 5.5f this year and another unraced daughter is the dam of two minor black type horses. There is another G1 Breeders Cup winner under the second dam in CALEDONIA ROAD (Quality Road) who won the G1 Breeders Cup Juvenile Fillies and was second in the G1 Frizette Stakes. Her sister Celestial is the dam of 2yo Pros And Cons (by Justify) who finished second in a Listed race first time out before winning second time out (entered in a stakes race on 04/09). Under the third dam this is also the family of G1 Winners HYMN BOOK and DATA LINK among other black type horses. This is a very good American pedigree with a good chance of further updates.

Nyquist was also a G1 Breeders Cup Juvenile winner before winning the Kentucky Derby and is one of the leading sires in the US. He has now had ten runners in Europe and CRIMSON ADVOCATE is the only black type to date. He has only had 52 runners from two crops to date as BMS, none of which are black type. His sire UNCLE MO was a top class US dirt stallion and also an excellent broodmare sire with 39 individual SWs and 7 G1WS with two SWs each by CANDY RIDE (sire of G1W GEAUX ROCKETS RIDE), INTO MISCHIEF and TWIRLING CANDY. He has had 13 runners in Europe as BMS, the best of which is 6F G3 winner CATCHING THE MOON by NO NAY NEVER.
plans2027.analysis:
NOT THIS TIME — I think this could be a great opportunity to use NOT THIS TIME whose stats are great and who is a big horse with lots of speed and already proven to work with the family as the sire of 2025 G1 Breeders Cup Turf winner CY FAIR out of a sister to CRIMSON ADVOCATE. His progeny appear to be effective both on dirt and turf which is the also the case for this family. There isn’t much to go on with yet with Nyquist as broodmare sire but NOT THIS TIME has sired G2W ON TIME GIRL and Stakes placed Turner’s Charm from 7 runners out of mares by his sire UNCLE MO.

JUSTIFY — This is another US alternative who is a top class stallion and very effective in Europe. He has had SW and G1P PRIVMAN as well as stakes placed Pronghorn from 9 runners out of UNCLE MO mares. From 2 runners from this family he has produced 2026 2yo Pros And Cons who was second in a stakes race on debut before wining impressively over a mile second time out. That said, it is under the second dam and although he is quite capable of producing precocious 2yos in spite of being a Triple Crown winner, he is not as much of an influence for speed as NOT THIS TIME.

FRANKEL — If you preferred to keep her in Europe, I think Frankel would probably be the best option again as she is a valuable mare and he is the best stallion in Europe. Although the cross is (not surprisingly) still unproven as her pedigree is largely an American dirt one, she was effective on turf and her dam won a stakes race on turf at two and he is the best stallion in Europe. Like his sire Galileo, he is very versatile and produces Group winners over every distance, although this year’s Group winners have been predominantly over Classic distances and he really excels as a sire of Classic horses.

mares.name: DARE TO DREAM
mares.physical: She is good looking and straightforward physically.

plans2027.raceRecord: A winner at two, three and four from 13 starts. She won a 1600m fillies’ newcomers in August on debut at Deauville on soft and was 3rd in an 8f Gr.3 at the Curragh, also on soft, from 3 starts at two. Won 3yo debut on heavy ground at Deauville, the 9f Gr.3 Prix Vanteaux. She was also fourth in the Alary (soft) and 5th in the Diane. Gr.3 her level and clearly kept for soft ground. She won a conditions on good to soft over a mile at four. Effective 8f-10f, soft ground specialist, genuine Gr.3 class and showed good form at two.
plans2027.pedigree: Beautifully bred, she is out of a Listed-placed Gold Away half-sister to Danedream, who was by Lomitas and clearly inherited stamina. She produced Illinois, Venice Beach and Broadway, all by Galileo and all decent middle-distance performers, though Broadway was 1m2f. So was Debutante, which explains this filly’s speedier profile. Camelots are not necessarily stout stayers. This is a lovely middle-distance page, and she is a little quicker than some of her talented close relatives.
plans2027.analysis: She is in foal to Sea The Stars, a cross that received a lovely boost in this year’s Derby - Christmas Day being bred on the reverse of it and the subsequent Gr.1 winner and runner-up Maltese Cross being by Sea The Stars and out of a Camelot mare. I think it will only get stronger. Night of Thunder was the second choice for her last year, largely because time was running out for Sea The Stars. He brings in the Galileo and is Mr Prospector line, which has a Gr.1 winner on the page, and Dubawi and Camelot have clicked from a very small sample - 8 foals for 2 SWs (25%). From four foals on the Night of Thunder x Camelot mares cross, there is the recent Gr.3 Prix de Cabourg winner and Gr.1 Prix Morny third Kosuma - also 25% SWs to foals. We know Night of Thunder works best with mares of her ilk, middle distance pedigree and 1m+ profile. Danedream was largely disappointing at stud, though her best horse Faylaq was by Dubawi. The fact that Galileo has worked so well with Danedrop too is encouraging for Night of Thunder. It makes a lot of sense for this to work. As he’s going to be oversubscribed, an alternative is required and I like Lope de Vega for her. She has speed but a classy middle-distance page. The very good looking and exciting Prix du Jockey Club winner Look De Vega is out of a High Chaparral mare (15% SWs to foals) and Lope de Vega with mares from that line have a decent list of success. Shadow Of Light is another top-class horse (ex New Approach mare). Lope and Camelot mares have 8 foals on the cross for one SW, I’d call that fine. You’d be hoping for a Classic type from this mating too if it went well.

plans2027.title: DARE TO DREAM 2021 by Camelot ex Debutante (Gold Away)
plans2027.raceRecord: 5yo mare and the winner of 3 races from 10 starts at 2 to 4 years including the Prix Vanteaux over 1800m. She also finished third in the G3 Staffordstown Stakes over a mile at two. She is now in foal for the first time to Sea The Stars - a cross which has worked out well this year with now 3 stakes horses from 3 runners including G1W MALTESE CROSS.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the fifth foal and only black type winner to date out of Debutante (Gold Away) who won over 2400m and was Listed placed over 1600m at three. Debutante is still at stud and there are seven fillies under the first dam, some of which have been well covered, so there could be more updates.

Debutante is a half sister to five time G1 DANEDREAM (Lomitas) as well as three further GWs in ILLINOIS, BROADWAY and VENICE BEACH (all by Galileo). Although it is a bit quieter under the third dam, this is a top class middle distance family and the fourth dam, G1W LADY BERRY, is responsible for numerous G1Ws including PLUMANIA, LEFT HAND and AVENTURE.

Camelot has had a very good year as BMS and his stats have leapt from 2% to 5% SW/Rs and a total of 14 SWs in 6 crops, including 2026 G1 Grand Prix De Paris winner MALTESE CROSS (by Sea The Stars) as well as 2yo G3 Prix De Cabourg winner KOSUMA and G3 winner MISS SCOTT (both by Night Of Thunder), which shows he is also very versatile. He is also the broodmare sire of recent G2 Futurity Stakes winner GIANT SEQUOIA by Frankel – his only runner on that cross. There have also been two individual SWs by Dubawi including G3W NEVER ENDING STORY. His own sire Montjeu was a good broodmare sire with 142 SWs (5%) including 18 G1Ws. His daughters did particularly well with DUBAWI (7SWs including G1W JOURNEY), KINGMAN (4 SWs including G1W FEED THE FLAME) and SIYOUNI (3 SWs including G1W PADDINGTON).
plans2027.analysis:
NIGHT OF THUNDER — As a G3W, she could be a good one for NIGHT OF THUNDER and the cross is now proven with G3W and G1 Prix Morny third KOSUMA who is bred similarly to her with Danehill also on the dam side, as well as G3W MISS SCOTT. Dare to Dream is inbred to Danehill and Night Of Thunder works very well with Danehill (36 SWs including G1Ws, PORTFOLIO DURATION, HIGHFIELD PRINCESS and OMBUDSMAN). Dubawi has also worked well with this family to produce G1W LEFT HAND and G2W PLUMATIC (albeit a different branch of the family)

She is correct and straightforward physically and benefits from a great first cover.

SEA THE STARS — If you prefer others for NIGHT OF THUNDER, this would still be a great cover and the cross has only strengthened since last year thanks to G1W MALTESE CROSS. He has the best statistics of the other European options and has already worked with the family to produce G1W AVENTURE (albeit from a slightly different branch)

LOPE DE VEGA — He's not quite in the same league as the two above but he is a very good stallion and reliable source of stakes winners. The direct cross has already produced a good filly and he has also been very effective with Montjeu (5 SWs) and his sons, and he also loves Danehill (14 G1Ws) to whom she is inbred.

mares.name: DRAMATISED
mares.physical: She was a top class sprinter and is an exciting young broodmare. She is a small compact mare who needs a big, rangy stallion. Her choice of stallion will largely depend on how much you like her young stock and in particular her Frankel foal.

plans2027.raceRecord: A very precocious juvenile, she was out before the end of April winning a 5f fillies’ maiden at Newmarket by 4l and followed up in the Gr.2 Queen Mary. Stepped up to 6f in the Gr.2 Lowther and ran with credit to finish 5th without seeing it out. She was an excellent second in the BC Juvenile Turf Sprint (5.5f) to Mischief Magic. She returned with a very impressive Gr.2 Temple Stakes win against seasoned older sprinters so you cannot say she didn’t train on. An out and out 5f filly, all her best runs were on G/F or good ground.
plans2027.pedigree: Daughter of Showcasing out of the 6f Listed Empress Stakes winner Katie’s Diamond, she was also 3rd in the Gr.3 7f Prix du Calvados and 5th, not beaten far, to Ballydoyle in the Gr.1 Poule d’Essai des Pouliches. There’s a US Stakes-winning miler on the page by Penny’s Picnic (son of Kheleyf), so this family has it in them to produce a miler by a quick sire. Showcasing is underperforming as a damsire but his first books were conceived quite cheaply, he has just 9 SWs in this role, the best being Lake Victoria, the brilliant daughter of Frankel and the x2 Gr.1-winning sprinter Quiet Reflection. There is also the Gr.3w History (Galileo) out of a Showcasing mare and the Gr.2 winner El Caballo by Havana Gold from the same sire line. Dramatised’s half-brother 2yo Hierax (Frankel) ran alright on debut. He was fifth in a hot Newmarket maiden behind the now-favourite for next year’s Guineas, Desert Castle (Frankel). A 425,000gns yearling, he’s with William Haggas so patience is to be expected and an improvement from first to second run.
plans2027.analysis: I mentioned Mehmas for her last year but I am just not hot on him any more for anything bar a 2yo. I think he is limited. These 5f mares are tricky if you are trying to breed Classic winners, which is why Frankel still makes the most sense. I am a fan of No Nay Never if you’re happy to breed a sprinter with precocity. He has such a good record at Ascot and really is the king of early speed and class as two. There is also always a remote chance you’ll get an Alcohol Free or a True Love. Alcohol Free actually comes from quite a quick family. True Love definitely gets help from Urban Sea. No Nay Never’s Libertango is out of an Oasis Dream mare (6 SWs from 31 foals for 19% SWs to foals). That said, her dam Katie’s Diamond being a half-sister to the dam of the Gr.2-winning miler Quattroelle by Mehmas, we could look at something like Blue Point, who is proven to get milers and out of a mare by Royal Applause so has some influence from the sire line. Blue Point and Oasis Dream mares are an excellent cross - from 29 foals there are four Stakes winners - 14% and includes the Gr.1 winner Big Evs and Gr.2 winners Elmonjed and Samangan. There is also the Gr.2 July Stakes winner Inner City Blues out of a Muhaarar mare, another son of Oasis Dream. Blue Point moves up his mares, but in order to get one that stays a mile, it looks as though he needs help from the dam. He won’t get that here, so we might be looking at a sprinter/2yo for all that Blue Point has shown he can get a top miler. As before, Frankel is perfect for her on paper, the cross, from a very small sample, gives no reason to knock it and he should complement her physically. Frankel typically brings the class and the mare tends to dictate the trip. That said, he is unlikely to ever sire a 5f sprinter and he’s the best option to try and produce a miler out of this filly, particularly with Lake Victoria in mind. Maybe see what the foal is like and repeat the dose unless you are keen for a change, in which case, my suggestion is Blue Point with No Nay Never as a second option.

plans2027.title: DRAMATISED 2020 by Showcasing ex Katie’s Diamond (Turtle Bowl)
plans2027.raceRecord: 6yo mare - 3 wins from 8 starts and 2 at 2 including the G2 Queen Mary Stakes over 5f. Also won the G2 Temple Stakes at three and runner up in the G1 Breeder’s Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the third foal out of her stakes winning dam and 2yo G3 placed dam KATIE’S DIAMOND (Turtle Bowl) who has produced two other winners and has subsequently been covered by Showcasing and Frankel, with a Frankel 2yo named Hierax who has run once, a yearling colt by Shaquille and a Frankel filly foal.

This is also the family of US G2 winner QUATTROELLE (Mehmas) who has a yearling and foal by Kitasan Black as well as G3 and dual stakes winner LES REYS (Penny’s Picnic) and four further stakes horses in Germany under the third dam. There is plenty of speed and precocity under the first two dams.

Although it is a different branch of the Green Desert line, he has also produced G2 Norfolk stakes winner SHAREHOLDER out of an Invincible Spirit mare.

FRANKEL — If you like her foal, all the reasons for going to him in the first place still stand. He is currently the best stallion in Europe and the cross has already produced G1 winner LAKE VICTORIA As well as 2026 group placed Minerva.

mares.name: EXXTRA
mares.physical: She needs a big, rangey, correct, stallion with a good temperament. If it weren't for that, she would be a good one for NIGHT OF THUNDER.

plans2027.raceRecord: A very tough mare, she won two Gr.3s and a Listed amongst 5 wins from 25 starts. She was out early, winning in April at two second time out (over 4.5f), and continued to progress each season. Effective 5-7f, she’s fast and classy. Also Gr.1-placed.
plans2027.pedigree: Starspangledbanner only has 315 foals of racing age as a damsire and 3 SWs to date, the impressive Gr.1 Phoenix Stakes winner Sun Goddess by Sioux Nation (his first Gr.1 winner), a Listed winner by Dark Angel and one by Night of Thunder. Her dam is a half-sister to the dam of one of Dark Angel’s best offspring - the sire and multiple Gr.1 winner Raging Bull and he is a half-brother to a Gr.3-winning sprinter by Dubawi. Her second dam was early and fast and held her form. It’s a very tough family and she was no exception. Dark Angel was champion sire two years ago but realistically he is past his best.
plans2027.analysis: Dubawi has a Gr.1-winning sprinter out of a Choisir mare, Creative Force (coincidentally his half-sister is the Gr.1 winner Persuasive, by Dark Angel). I saw him at Darley’s stallion parade and he looked great and showed no signs of age. She’s in foal on an early cover so presumably was straightforward. I haven’t seen her but if she is typical of Starspangledbanner I envisage a strong, heavy-set mare and I am not sure that’s the way forward for Night of Thunder. It’s also not the most obvious for Dubawi in fairness, which is why I am including Kingman again for her. I think a tough and sound mare like her is exactly what suits Kingman and he is a finer type who benefits from a mare with substance. In terms of the physical, I would leave that to you as you know them. There is nothing on the cross with Kingman and just Creative Force by Dubawi out of a mare by Choisir. Simply because he is the better sire, Dubawi edges it over Kingman but both would be excellent options. She is in foal to Frankel and that was the first selection last year. There is no reason not to repeat it if you like the foal. Starspangledbanner has always worked exceptionally well as a sire with Sadler’s Wells line mares, it’s actually staggering how good it is. Precise is by SSB out of a Galileo mare. I think it is due in part to Sadler’s Wells quality complementing SSB substance. In essence, it is Galileo and Danehill, which was why Frankel made perfect sense and should hopefully produce a Guineas-class progeny.

plans2027.raceRecord: 6yo mare and the winner of 5 races from 23 starts. She won second time out over 4 ½ furlongs in April at two and has won two G3s over 6f and 7f at three and four, as well as picking up many places including 2nd place in the G1 Maurice De Gheest in 2024. She is in foal for the first time to Frankel.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the third foal and only black type filly to date out of Rolling Stone, a placed daughter of ROLLY POLLY who won 10 races including the G2 Prix Robert Papin and also finished third in the G1 Prix Morny. Rolling Stone’s sister Rosa Bonheur (Mr Greeley) was Listed placed before producing triple G1 winner RAGING BULL (Dark Angel) and 2yo G3W KUBRICK (Dubawi). Her 3yo half brother Hendrixx (City Light) is a winner and she has a 2yo brother by Saxon Warrior (bought back as a yearling for €17,000) as well as a yearling sister by Hello Youmzain.

Starspangledbanner has had an amazing year as a sire and an improved year as broodmare sire. He is now the broodmare sire of G1 winning 2yo filly SUN GODDESS (by Sioux Nation) as well as recent G3 Prix de Meautry winner GREAT WISH (by Night Of Thunder). Added to that, he is also the broodmare sire of this year’s G2 Railway Stakes third Confucius (by No Nay Never). In total he has now had 3 SWs and 7 stakes placed horses from 167 starters.

Second damsire Raven’s Pass is a good broodmare sire with 28 SWs from 530 runners (5%) in 11 crops including 4 G1Ws. Two of these are from the Dubawi line with MISHRIFF (Make Believe) and SAFFRON BEACH (New Bay). Dubawi himself has produced G3W DUBAWI LEGEND from just two runners out of Raven’s Pass mares and NIGHT OF THUNDER has produced 2 SWs from 4 runners on the same cross (albeit in Sweden and Italy). That said, he is very versatile with his 14 Group winners by 14 different stallions and his 28 stakes winners by 26 different stallions. This year he is the broodmare sire of G2 German 1000 Guineas winner TIMEFORSHOWASING (Showcasing).
plans2027.analysis:
JUSTIFY — He is from the same Scat Daddy sireline as 2yo G2W SUN GODDESS (Sioux Nation) and 2yo G2 placed Confucius (No Nay Never), both of which are out of Starspangledanner mares.

This year’s 2yos from his fifth crop are already confirming he is in the elite league and he can produce top class horses from Ascot 2yos to Gold Cup winners. He has already worked with the Danehill line more generally including with Danehill Dancer - 3 SWs including G1W OPERA SINGER (second dam by Danehill Dancer) as well as Chesham Stakes debut runner up On Just Terms). He has also worked with the Raven’s Pass/Elusive Quality line and both RAMATUELLE and HARD TO JUSTIFY are out of speedy mares which is also encouraging.

NOT THIS TIME — Not unlike Dramatised, he should be not only be a good fit physically but also a good speed option if you wanted to zero in on the speed in this family. She won in April as a 2yo over 900 metres and is a Group winner over six and seven furlongs. Her grand dam was second in the G1 Prix Morny. Although the direct cross is not proven, he has had a G3 winner out of a mare with Choisir as second broodmare sire.

plans2027.raceRecord: A winner on debut in May over 7f at Haydock (good to firm), she was second in the Listed Star Stakes (soft), won the Gr.3 Sweet Solera Stakes and Gr.1 Moyglare Stakes (good to yielding). Given she stayed a mile well at two, I think she would’ve stayed further and that Too Darn Hot has put the speed into Fallen Angel. Agnes was out of a 1m4f Dalakhani mare and her half-sister by Dansili stayed 1m5f.
plans2027.analysis: Given she is a proper miler and from a family with class and stamina, Frankel makes perfect sense. Too Darn Hot has no record yet as a damsire but daughters of his sire Dubawi have an excellent record with Frankel - 15 SWs for 12% strike rate, many high-class ones, and we know the sire lines complement each other. The resulting mating would have a Classic pedigree.

mares.physical: Lengthy, perhaps a bit short of leg. Height preferred, particularly for first foal She sounds quite Dark Angel physically and seems at least for a 1st cover a stallion with leg is preferred. There is really not much between these two choices on paper but physically it sounds like Frankel could have the edge.

plans2027.raceRecord: A high-class sprinter. She made her debut in May at two, ran creditably in the Hilary Needler and Queen Mary and then bolted up in the Alice Keppel (5f) at Goodwood. She was proper 5f at two, second in the Flying Childers. At three she wanted 6f, winning the Gr.3 Summer Stakes and was 3/4l 3rd in the Champions Sprint to Kind Of Blue. She didn’t win at four but again was classy in defeat, second to Inisherin in the Duke of York, third to Lazzat and to Big Mojo at Royal Ascot and Haydock respectively. Seems as good as ever at five, won three of five, only defeat when stalls got the better of her and when not showing in the City of York. Conceded a penalty when winning the Oak Tree Stakes over 7f. Lots of 7f entries now, she deserves a Gr.1.
plans2027.pedigree: Flora's dam was bred for speed (Cadeaux Genereux) though won over a mile. The second dam stayed 10f, probably the Silver Hawk influence as Flora's third dam was a champion sprinter. There is some evidence in the pedigree to suggest this family throws to the stallion, Powerful Breeze just failed by a head in the Fillies’ Mile and is by Iffraaj, and her dam Power Of Light stayed a mile and is by Echo Of Light. The third dam Flowing was a champion sprinter in Ireland.
plans2027.analysis: We’ve looked at Night of Thunder for her and now she has proven she is more than 5f/6f, statistically I can be happy with it. It’s the same cross as new Gr.1 winner Ten Bob Tony, the only Stakes winner on the cross from 16 foals. His dam actually stayed 1m4f and is from a Classic distance family. Bow Echo is still the only Gr.1 winner by Night of Thunder out of a sprinter (6f), though he is from the Italian Oaks family of Zomaradah and the miler Dubawi himself. Gewan was out of a mare by Dark Angel's son Lethal Force, though she was best at a mile. In terms of the cross, I think it is fine. Night of Thunder has a couple of new Group winners this year from speedier families. The Gr.3 winner Evolutionist didn't stay 1m2f in the Diane, she is out of a Showcasing mare who won over 7f. The Gr.2 winner Zeus Olympios is from a quicker family, 7f/8f, and we've mentioned Bow Echo. She has so much class and the cross looks good based on what we’ve seen so far. Bow Echo is out of a 6f mare as we've mentioned, so I could not say no to it but in terms of a perfect pedigree fit, it just misses based on what Night of Thunder has really clicked with elsewhere. However, she is a high-class filly, the cross seems to work and you can make a case based on Bow Echo, who likewise is out of a mare who was dominated by her sire Invincible Spirit and not by the Classic pedigree behind her. The ‘best’ you could hope for is a top-class miler, that may well be a sprinter. If it has class I wouldn't be trying anything like the Evolutionist team did in the Diane. As an alternative, I propose Kingman for her. He has a Listed winner on the cross from 8 foals (13%) and you have mentioned before Kingman does well with a mare that needs some leg and a shorter back. She seems very durable, very tough and sound. There is the stalls quirk but that’s not a reason to think she is mentally not for Kingman. He imparts speed and class and the offspring could sprint but reasonably could well see out a mile.

She is the 8th of ten foals out of dual winner Dubai Power (Cadeaux Genereux) whose other black type progeny is Stakes placed Power Of Light (Echo Of Light) who is also the dam of G2 winning 2yo and G1 Fillies Mile runner up POWERFUL BREEZE (Iffraaj). Second dam Garmoucheh was stakes placed over 7 furlongs and her one black type offspring was stakes placed Vanguard Dream who was also stakes placed over 7 furlongs. Third dam is Champion Older Female Sprinter FLOWING who won the G3 Flying Five Stakes twice and whose offspring include the dams of US G2W STORM MESA and SW SHE BE CLASSY.

Dark Angel has had 28 SWs from 883 runners and 11 crops as BMS. His three G1 winners include 2026 G1 Queen Anne Stakes winner TEN BOB TONY (Night Of Thunder), G1 winning sprinter HAVANA GREY (by Havana Gold from the Galileo line) as well as Yorkshire Oaks winner CONTENT (Galileo) whose sister BEDTIME STORY (Frankel) is a G2W and G1 placed. In 2025 he was also the broodmare sire of G2 May Hill Stakes winner AYLIN (St Marks Basilica) as well as G3 winner RED LETTER who is also by Frankel, making it two stakes winners on that direct cross. He is also the broodmare sire of SW CAJOLE by Dubawi, G3W CRESTA by New Bay and SW CHELSEA BELIEVE by Make Believe - all from the Dubawi line.
plans2027.analysis:
FRANKEL — There is really not much in this and it is a bit of a physical preference (and I haven’t even seen her!). He does still have the best statistics in Europe and the direct cross has produced 2 GWs and 4 further stakes horses from 15 runners including promising Listed placed 2yo Maire Rua. Dark Angel mares have also worked with Galileo more generally, and although the links start to get more tenuous, G1W VERACIOUS also has Cadeaux Genereux as a second dam sire.

His 14% SW/R strike rate is already excellent and like to keep improving given the books he has been covering in recent years and the fact that his sibling comparison stats are excellent. He has produced G1 Queen Anne Stakes winner TEN BOB TONY from 10 runners out of Dark Angel mares. 2yo G1W GEWAN is also out of a Lethal Force mare from the same sire line and G3Ws FAIRY GODMOTHER and ROMANTIC STYLE both have Cadeaux Genereux on their dam side.

NOT THIS TIME — She could easily go to America to this top class stallion with plenty of speed and whose only runner out of an Acclamation mare is a stakes winner but I think unless there is a physical need, the two stallions above are already both such good options this is very much third best.

Dubawi’s ever expanding sire line is also on the mark - Dubawi (1 SW from 6 foals), New Bay (1 SW from 7 foals), Night of Thunder (1 SW from 6 foals) and Make Believe (1 SW from 3 foals). Looking at Dark Angel’s record in this role, there isn’t one particular stallion or line which works. The first of Dark Angel’s increased fee crops are only just starting to have daughters old enough to produce runners. His first properly expensive crop, €60k fee in 2016, had daughters old enough to have 3yos last year, so his record should be improving but at the moment it has not. Nakuti also won the Atalanta Stakes and her two-year-old, Heredia’s full-brother The Big Con, was unbeaten in two starts in Canada at two, including a Gr.3, and returned with a creditable fifth in the Gr.1 Saratoga Derby on 8th August. Heredia is Nakuti’s first foal and the pedigree is active. Her half-brother Amade won the 2m Gr.2 Belmont Gold Cup and Gr.3 Geelong Cup. He’s by Casamento, a moderate son of Shamardal but Storm Cat line sire, like Justify. There’s a bit more stamina further down the page than you might initially think, probably why Heredia got a mile so well for a Dark Angel. There’s also a mix of dirt and turf, so if you wanted to race the progeny in the US that would be fine.
plans2027.analysis: She is in foal to Justify on a late cover. She has the right distance profile and pedigree for him and as mentioned, Dark Angel daughters as yet offer no strong guidance as to what works best. She is currently in America and you have mentioned Not This Time, who I am a fan of and he hails from the same sire line as Justify, which suits her. Not This Time is more of a speed influence than Justify, which is fine for her as she is quick but does have some stamina on the page. Like Justify, the foal will also be (almost) completely free of Northern Dancer in the first 5 generations (Not This Time is 4th generation ND), so has an ideal stallion or broodmare’s pedigree if inheriting either parent’s ability. In terms of Europe, Frankel has to be first choice. Dark Angel’s only real record with his daughters and a sire line is this one. Gr.1 winner Content and Gr.2 winner Bedtime Story are both out of a very good mare by Dark Angel, which the foal would also be. Frankel has 2 SWs from 25 foals on the cross for an 8% strike rate. It’s not particularly strong but at the moment Dark Angel is a disappointing damsire so it makes sense to go where there has been some success. Her half-sister by Night of Thunder isn’t up to much so we can leave him for the moment. Frankel makes more sense on pedigree.

plans2027.raceRecord: 7yo mare and the winner of 7 races from 2 to 6. Her best performance is a win in the G2 Yellow Ribbon Handicap over 1m 1/2 f at Del Mar in 2025, but she also won her first four races including two at two in the UK as well as a Listed race and the G3 Atalanta Stakes over a mile at Sandown at four. She is in foal for the first time to Justify
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the first foal out of NAKUTI (by Mastercraftsman) who also won the G3 Atalanta Stakes as well as three other races from 7 f to 1 mile. Heredia’s 3yo full brother THE BIG CON (Dark Angel) won the G3 Grey Stakes at Woodbine last year and her 4yo sister VRONTI (Night Of Thunder) recently won a stakes race at Del Mar over 2200m. Nakuti is a half sister to AMADE who won 11 races including the G2 Belmont Gold Cup and they are out of a sister to 8 time winner and multiple stakes winners ARCH REBEL and ON MY DIME as well as the dam of 5 time winner and G3 winner CUSTOMER BASE and a host of further black type horses. The best horses in this family have been very tough and durable and Nakuti is turning into an amazing broodmare.

Dark Angel has had 28 SWs from 883 runners and 11 crops as BMS. His three G1 winners include 2026 G1 Queen Anne Stakes winner TEN BOB TONY (Night Of Thunder), G1 winning sprinter HAVANA GREY (by Havana Gold from the Galileo line) as well as Yorkshire Oaks winner CONTENT (Galileo) whose sister BEDTIME STORY (Frankel) is a G2W and G1 placed. plans2027.analysis:

Added to that, Night Of Thunder has also worked with second dam sire Mastercraftsman to produce G3 WKON TIKI and G3 placed Queen Of Thunder from 5 runners and he works extremely well with Danehill more generally including G1Ws OMBUDSMAN, HIGHFIELD PRINCESS and PORTFOLIO DURATION.

plans2027.raceRecord: Won her only start at two in December on AW over 9.5f and a 9f Listed the following May by 4.5L. She then placed twice in Gr.3s and won the Gr.3 Bertrand de Tarragon (9f) on her last start in France, again by a wide margin. She ran 12 times in the US, only once out of the 1st four, and signed off with an 8.5f allowance win. She has placed four times in Gr.3s, three times on a firm track and over 11f, once she had yielding ground over 12f, but it was her weakest performance of the four. So it was not the firm ground stopping her get her head in front. She is effective 8.5f-11f, coming within a neck of winning a Gr.3 over 11f. plans2027.analysis: Lawman gets a lot of winners as a damsire, not so many Stakes winners. He has three new ones this year to date and so now has 27. He has been a disappointment as a stallion, so his daughters probably haven’t had much opportunity. Enough of his SWs as a damsire are Group winners though (12 of 27), so though inconsistent, there is some quality. We liked Justify partially because of Storm Cat, which brings Not This Time into the reckoning should you not wish to repeat the dose. There are five SWs by Storm Cat line sons out of Lawman mares, four Listed level but with Group form, and the Gr.2 Italian Oaks winner. Three are by Lope de Vega, one by Caravaggio and one by Footstepsinthesand (Gr.2w). Unsurprisingly, the cross is largely untried, but like with Circios, Immensitude is by a son of Invincible Spirit, who is the damsire of Shareholder. If she were to come back to Europe, she is the type of mare I would send to Night of Thunder. She has the right profile and her family is middle-distance. Lawman mares and Night of Thunder have just seven foals, five have run and four have won, including the Gr.3 Autumn Stakes winner Hankelow. Invincible Spirit mares have fared a little better, and that is saying something as they are no good, and there are 3 SWs, including Bow Echo. What is interesting about Bow Echo is that he is also from a top-class 1m-1m2f family (that of Dubawi). Despite Green Desert line sires underwhelming to date with Night of Thunder, this is a mare who should work with him and has the right profile.

plans2027.title: IMMENSITUDE 2020 by Lawman ex Ma Petite Poule (Elusive City))
plans2027.raceRecord: 6yo mare and the winner of 4 races from 20 starts. She then went to the US where she was placed four times at Group level over 1m3f. She is in foal for the first time to Justify.
plans2027.pedigree:
IMMENSITUDE is the third of seven foals and only black type horse to date out of Ma Petite Poule (Elusive City) who won three races from 1500m to 1900m. The second dam produced G3W REMUS DE LA TOUR (Stormy River) as well as SW and G3P CHILL (Verglas), whose line continues via SW CHILDA (Duke Of Marmalade) and GWs CHILEAN (Iffraaj) and PRINCESS CHILD (Dariyan). Under the fourth dam, this is also the family of numerous G1 winners including AUGUSTE RODIN, MAGICAL and RHODODENDRON.

Lawman is a fair broodmare sire with 27 SWs from 790 runners (3%) in 12 crops. In the last 12 months G3W HANKELOW (Night Of Thunder) is the most significant stakes horse to have added to his numbers. It now makes the Dubawi sireline quite significant as he has had 4 individual SWs from that sireline – G1W FALLEN ANGEL (Too Darn Hot) G2W PURPLEPAY (Zarak) and NASHA NASHA (Dubawi). As well as Night Of Thunder whose broodmare sire is Galileo, he has 4 stakes winners by different stallions from the Galileo line (Cracksman, Australia, Frankel, Gleneagles). He has had Group winning siblings BATTAASH and THE ANTARCTIC from 21 runners by Dark Angel and three SWs from 22 runners by LOPE DE VEGA (none of which are Group winners).

plans2027.analysis:
NIGHT OF THUNDER — I think she could be a lovely one for NIGHT OF THUNDER as the direct cross has worked already and he has also produced multiple G1W BOW ECHO out of a mare by his sire Invincible Spirit. Added to that, Lawman has worked well as a broodmare sire with other stallions from both the Dubawi and the Galileo line. More generally, Invincible Spirit has worked well with Dubawi including G1Ws NOTABLE SPEECH and OPERA BALLO (similar Dubawi/Galileo cross).

NOT THIS TIME — If you prefer to keep her in the US, this would be a good option. He is proving to be a really top class, versatile stallion effective both on turf and dirt and has already worked well with European turf bloodlines including Invincible Spirit, having produced Ascot 2yo G2 Norfolk Stakes winner SHAREHOLDER. Although SHAREHOLDER won over 5f and some of Not This Time’s progeny are very fast, they are effective over a range of distances up to 1m2f. He has also proved effective with ELUSIVE QUALITY (sire of Elusive City) on the dam side with three stakes winners and a further G1 placed Blackout Time from just 21 runners.

FRANKEL — She could also be one for Frankel as she is good looking and is a multiple Group performer with enough speed. His record with Lawman mares and with Invincible Spirit more generally is good rather than great but maybe one should not overthink that as she was a tough and talented race mare and it is not known to be the strongest broodmare sireline to date.

Given the anticipated issues with him, his son Night of Thunder is the no.1 choice, he’s had four Stakes winners out of Sea The Stars mares. Her physical should suit too, being a correct mare with a big walk who is good head on.

plans2027.title: INFINITE COSMOS 2020 by Sea The Stars ex Waila (Notnowcato)
plans2027.raceRecord: 6yo chestnut mare in foal for the second time to Justify. She won once and placed four times from just five starts including being G3 placed in the Musidora Stakes (10 ½ f) at three and G2 placed in the Middleton at four (10 ½ f).
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the fourth of nine foals and best flat performer to date out of WAILA (Notnowcato) who won the Listed Aphrodite stakes over 1m4f. Her bother HAVAILA (Le Havre) is a very useful dual purpose horse and the winner of a G3 chase. This is a top class middle distance family with three G1Ws under the first three dams. The second dam CRYSTAL CAVERN produced 8 winners Including CRYSTAL STAR (Mark Of Esteem) the dam of G1Ws CRYSTAL OCEAN (Sea The Stars), HILLSTAR (Danehill Dancer), G2 winner CRYSTAL CAPELLA (Cape Cross) as well as stakes winner CRYSTAL ZVEDZA (Dubawi). There has been a stakes update in Australia this year thanks to SW KINGS VALLEY (by Territories) who is a grandson of Crystal Cavern.

Sea The Stars is an excellent broodmare sire with 7% SW/Rs from 10 crops and 9 SWs including 12 G1Ws and 2026 Derby winner CHRISTMAS DAY (by Camelot). His daughters have a very good strike rate with Dubawi with 5 individual SWs from 16 runners (31%) including G1Ws ELDAR ELDAROV and AL HUSN. They also now have 4 individual SWs from 22 runners by his son NIGHT OF THUNDER including 2026 G3W AMBERGLEN. In spite of the inbreeding, the Kingman/Sea The Stars cross goes from strength to strength with 6 individual SWs and a really great 24% strike rate. He has also produced two G1 winners by Frankel [ONESTO and EL CORDOBES] albeit with a lower strike rate of 13% SW/R. He appears to be very versatile as a broodmare sire with stakes winners by 35 different stallions ranging from Mehmas to Le Havre.

Another top class middle distance breeding prospect. She has had two very good covers and a lot will depend on what her first foal is like.
plans2027.analysis:
CAMELOT — I know it looks like I've seen CHRISTMAS DAY and made a lazy decision on that basis - but although his statistics are not in the same league as a couple of other options but she is a lovely middle distance prospect from a family with plenty of stamina and I feel CAMELOT would give her every chance of breeding a Derby or St Leger winner rather than a middle of the range stakes winner over a shorter distance. Less and less horses are bred for those distances and there is real opportunity there, particularly with a mare with this type of pedigree. He is also out of a Kingmambo mare and there is a huge affinity between the two stallions with 5 G1Ws bred on the Sea The Stars / Kingmambo cross.

LOPE DE VEGA — Although he is not quite the top class influence that some of the other stallions are, this mating avoids close inbreeding and is not just a proven direct cross but there also a well established affinity between the Shamardal and Cape Cross lines including 2026 G1W ALMAQAM. He is also proven to work well with more middle distance bloodlines. BEAUVATIER is out of a mare who was Listed placed over 10 ½ furlongs from a middle distance family.

NIGHT OF THUNDER — I dithered about including him because of the inbreeding and because I wasn't convinced it was a great cross (hasn’t produced a G1W yet) but AMBERGLEN looks like a good filly and it is quite hard to overlook him when he is such a good stallion and it is quite hard to say a cross has not worked when it has produced four stakes winners [albeit not his best). Interestingly, Night Of Thunder’s strike rate with Cape Cross mares is only 1 SW from 21 runners although that stakes winner is G1 winner THUNDERING NIGHTS.

mares.name: JASNA'S SECRET
mares.physical: Looking at her photo she looks small and strong and will need a stallion with size and leg.

plans2027.raceRecord: She won her first two starts at two over 6f and disappointed in the Cheveley Park Stakes. She won a 6f Listed at 3 and 7f Listed this term and looks genuine Listed class.
plans2027.pedigree: Her dam won at two and is a half-sister to a Listed-winning miler by Zamindar, who then went to Invincible Spirit and produced a Listed winner, the same cross as Kingman himself. The pedigree hasn’t really moved since last year and there is not much to go on. Galiway is unproven as a damsire with just 27 foals of racing age and still Campacite (Zarak, Listed winner and Gr.1-placed at two) his only SW in this role.
plans2027.analysis: Jasna’s Secret is quite fast. Without anything new to go on from her own family, the magical cross with Galileo mares, as we know, is Justify and he goes one step further than Lope de Vega (the European suggestion) in that he seems to click particularly well with Sadler’s Wells line mares. Galiway daughters should be no exception. We know Justify is better with a quicker mare, though he works with a variety, and imparts stamina so she has the right fit for him. She is from the right sire line, she was precocious and she has the speed and class to suit him. Lope de Vega is another stallion to do particularly well with Galileo mares and is capable of getting good 2yos that progress at three. Similar to sending her to Kingman, you could hope for a miler with precocity from this mating, if you want to keep her in Europe.

Under the third dam this is also the family of a number of stakes winners including multiple G1W IRESINE.

Galiway is young as a broodmare sire and covered small numbers of mares to start with so has only had 15 runners as BMS but these include 2yo SW and G1 runner up CAMPACITE (ZARAK) who has been placed at Group level this year at three. It’s not enough to make a statistic but also nice to know he has already produced a good horse from small opportunities. BLUE POINT — I feel he could work really well as she had lots of speed and although he has sired G1 winning miler ROSALLION out of a New Approach mare, he is ultimately more of a speed stallion. plans2027.analysis: She was on the list for Night of Thunder, whose progeny progress and ought to help her out as she didn’t for whatever reason, but clearly had ability. There is not much to take from Kendargent’s record as a damsire given the stallions his daughters have visited, many have gone to Guy Pariente’s own Galiway. He has 21 SWs in this role, two Gr.1 winners by Galiway, nine SWs overall. We’re looking for a sire whose offspring progress and are consistent and work with mile plus mares and though Night of Thunder has no foals of racing age out of Kendargent mares, that doesn’t worry me. Time Test has the Listed winner Betty Clover out of a Kendargent mare, that’s about all there is on the cross. I also put Justify as an option for her last year and that still stands. plans2027.title: JULICA 2021 by Kendargent ex Miss Rail Link (Rail Link)
plans2027.raceRecord: 5yo mare and the winner of four races from 9 starts. She won three races at two over a mile, including a Listed race on soft ground in November. She also won over 2100m in Qatar at four and is now in foal for the first time to Frankel.
plans2027.pedigree:
JULICA is the fifth foal out of MISS RAIL LINK who won five races from 2400m to 4200m including over jumps. She is a sister to three winners including multiple stakes placed Aude (Shamalgan). The second dam PLAYACT is a Listed winner over 2000m and was placed at Group level including twice finishing second at G2 level in the US. She is the dam of five winners including two black type National Hunt horses. This is also the family of G3W BREATHTAKING LOOK (Bated Breath). The family is a bit dead but it does include 2025 2yo stakes winner ARAGUM BAY (Soldier’s Call) under the third dam.

Kendargent is a solid broodmare sire with 21 SWs from 423 runners (4%) in 11 crops. Both his own sire and broodmare sire Kendor and Linamix were also good broodmare sires which is encouraging for JULICA. He has had one SW this year as BMS, namely German G2W ENGLISHMAN by Nathaniel. There are now 75 runners bred on the Galiway/Kendor cross with 6 SWs including G1 winners SEALIWAY and SUNWAY. There have also been two stakes winners by STYLE VENDOME all bred by the same person. The other 12 SWs have all been by different stallions but do include SW RESTIANY as well as two further stakes placed horses by FRANKEL (same Galileo/Danehill cross as Galiway) from 7 horses on that cross.
plans2027.analysis:
NIGHT OF THUNDER — He has gone from strength to strength this year and having had one great cover to Frankel, she could be a good one for him. Although the direct cross is not proven, he is incredibly versatile and has a good strike rate with Kendor on the dam side. Added to that, he does love Dansili mares (sire of Rail Link) and now has 10 SWs in total from 45 runners with Dansili on the dam side including G1Ws OMBUDSMAN and PORTFOLIO DURATION.

FRANKEL — Kendargent’s 2026 G2 winner by Nathaniel makes the decision to go to Frankel first time look great as does the fact that he now has 14 SWs from 95 runners with Dansili on the dam side including G1Ws ITEM, MINNIE HAUK and SOUL SISTER (though none yet with Rail Link from 4 runners). I don't really think the fact that Kendargent mares have worked with Galiway is necessarily relevant [unless that is the reason for his success!) but it doesn't harm to know a similar cross has worked well - though those SWs were not inbred to Danehill.

plans2027.title: LADY VIVIAN 2022 by Camelot ex Ceol an Ghra (Teofilo)
plans2027.raceRecord: 4yo filly and the winner of 2 races at three in 11 starts from 2 to 4 years. including the Prix Vanteaux over 1800m. She finished second in the Listed Prix Panacee over 2400m at three and was also second in the Listed Coral Marathon over 2 miles at Sandown.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the third of five foals and the only black type filly to date out of the winning mare CEOL AN GHRA who is 13 and has been covered by Coolmore stallions including producing two full sisters, neither of which are winners. CEOL AN GHRA is a sister to the dam of G1W LOCH GARMAN (also by Teofilo) as well as the dam of G3W and G1 Irish 1000 Guineas runner up REHN’S NEST (Authorized). Under the third dam this is also the family of G1 winning 2yo EVA LUNA (Double Schwartz), G2 winning 2yo BEACON (Paco Boy) and G3 winning 2yo COIS NA TINE (Double Schwartz) so although she was a stayer there is plenty of speed and precocity further back in her family.

Camelot has had great a year as BMS and his stats have leapt from 2% to 5% SW/Rs and a total of 14 SWs in 6 crops, including 2026 G1 Grand Prix De Paris winner MALTESE CROSS (by Sea The Stars) as well as 2yo G3 Prix De Cabourg winner KOSUMA and G3 winner MISS SCOTT (both by Night Of Thunder), which shows he is also very versatile. He is also the broodmare sire of recent G2 Futurity Stakes winner GIANT SEQUOIA by Frankel – his only runner on that cross. There have also been two individual SWs by Dubawi including G3W NEVER ENDING STORY. His own sire Montjeu was a good broodmare sire with 142 SWs (5%) including 18 G1Ws. His daughters did particularly well with DUBAWI (7SWs including G1W JOURNEY), KINGMAN (4 SWs including G1W FEED THE FLAME) and SIYOUNI (3 SWs including G1W PADDINGTON).

She has two strands of Sadler's Wells and Danehill already so I would probably be cautious of adding any more.
plans2027.analysis:
LOPE DE VEGA — On paper, I think he would suit her really well as not only has the direct cross worked already but he has also worked more generally with Montjeu line mares and has also worked with second damsire Teofilo to produce 6 SWs including G1 winner DREAMLOPER. She has two strands of both Sadler's Wells and Danehill and he is known to work well with both. Also, although she had plenty of stamina [probably thanks to Camelot], further back this is a family with speed too and he is versatile enough to work with both.

KINGMAN — Although he has only had two runners out of Camelot mares, he has produced some very good horses out of Montjeu mares including G1 Grand Prix De Paris winner FEED THE FLAME. He is another stallion who works well with mares with more stamina as well as the speedier ones. He has produced SW VICTORY QUEEN and two further stakes horses out of Teofilo mares and has worked very well with Galileo more generally including G1Ws COMMISSIONING and SPARKLING PLENTY (ex Frankel mare). I'm not as convinced he works so well with Danehill in spite of G1W PERSIAN KING (ex Dylan Thomas mare) but he has had plenty of Group winners (such as SPARKLING PLENTY) with Danehill further back on the dam side.

SEA THE STARS — I just thought he was worth having on the list as in spite of the slightly ugly inbreeding, he is such a good stallion and will not be around forever. She is young and the cross has worked very well including G1W MALTESE CROSS as well as with Montjeu more generally. There is speed further back in the family and if you're not afraid of breeding a stayer it might be a good opportunity to use him this year before he gets too old. He is one year older than LOPE DE VEGA.

plans2027.raceRecord: A winner on debut at Nottingham over 5f on good to firm in June, she followed up in the Gr.2 Queen Mary Stakes (good to firm). She was third in the Gr.2 Lowther Stakes (good to firm) and last in the Gr.1 Cheveley Park Stakes (soft), all her starts at two. She made a promising return to action in the Listed Achillies Stakes, the only three-year-old in the race, where she was fourth without a clear run, back over 5f (good) and was not seen again until she finished 4th in Listed company on AW as a four-year-old in Feb and subsequently had a wind op. She went to Ascot and disappointed in a handicap and was well beaten in the Gr.3 Coral Charge as well before retirement.
plans2027.pedigree: She is the best of two winners out of the Dandy Man half-sister to the Listed City Plate (x2) winner Majestic Myles (Majestic Missile), a 7f specialist who was tough and sound, and a full-sister to the Gr.2 Coventry and Listed Surrey Stakes second, Gr.2 Gimcrack and Vintage Stakes third Parbold. Kassandra’s half-sister Oonagh (Arakan) produced the Listed winning sprinter and subsequently Gr.3-winning miler Power Under Me (Mehmas). Right back on the page is her wonderful fourth dam, the champion Talking Picture, responsible for a dynasty of talented middle-distance and staying horses, namely Kyprios, Search For A Song, Free Eagle et al.
plans2027.analysis: I don’t mind sending sprinters to Frankel, he’s had the likes of Lake Victoria, Chaldean, Benvenuto Cellini, Diego Velazquez etc. out of quicker or speedily bred mares to name a few. I also like that Galileo has worked so well with her family and also that she has that Classic class in her family, albeit distantly. Things didn’t work out for her after Ascot, but she showed enough on her return at three to suggest she wasn’t just early speed to my eye. Frankel has no record with Kodi Bear mares but does have a Gr.3 winner Perfect News out of the Queen Mary third Besharah (Kodiac) and Gr.2-placed Central Europe out of the Queen Mary second Tiggy Wiggy. Having seen her at Royal Ascot, I think Frankel could put some size into her, not that she lacks substance, but a bit of scope and the offspring should have no issue with a mile.

plans2027.title: LOPE DE LILAS 2021 by Lope De Vega ex Golden Gazelle (Galileo)
plans2027.raceRecord: 5yo racemare and the winner of one race over 10 furlongs at three from 8 starts from 2 to 4. She must have been highly rated as she ran third time out in the Irish Oaks, finishing 11th behind YOU GOT TO ME. She did not win again but she did finish second on her reappearance in April 2025 and was rated 92.
plans2027.pedigree:
LOPE DE LILAS is the second of six foals out of GOLDEN GAZELLE [Galileo] who was herself a winner over 10 furlongs. She also finished fourth twice at Listed level in Germany and Italy. Golden Gazelle is a daughter of the top class GREYS LILAS (Danehill) who won four races including the G1 Prix du Moulin and went on to produce three time G1 winner GOLDEN LILAC (by Galileo and a full sister to Golden Gazelle) as well as G3 and multiple stakes winner GREY LION (also by Galileo) as well as stakes winner GOLDEN GUEPARD (by Hurricane Run) and the dam of stakes winner and G2 placed PALOMBE (Nathaniel). Third dam KENMIST was a stakes winner and went on to produce 4 stakes horses in total as well as the dams of G3 winner CLOUDY DAWN and stakes winner IROMEA.

Lope de Vega is a very good broodmare sire with 31 SWs from 619 runners (5%) in 9 crops. The best of these are 2026 G1 winners BENVENUTO CELLINI and ITEM (both by Frankel) – a cross which has produced 3 SWs in total from just 6 runners to date also including Benvenuto Cellini’s sister SW Giselle. He also has two stakes winners apiece by Siyouni (25%) and New Bay (11%), But other than that his 31 stakes winners are all by different stallions ranging from middle distance stallions such as Camelot and Nathaniel to Sprint sires such as Kodiac and Mehmas.

Lope Des Lilas is very big, heavy and a bit plain and needs a neat horse with class. She has a lovely page and is a very nice prospect at stud although I would be mindful that there is only white type under the first dam at the moment. As she is out of a Galileo mare, I would rule out that line at the moment to avoid inbreeding.
plans2027.analysis:
CAMELOT — I am putting him down as an option in spite of the inbreedings, or in his case because of the inbreedings, as he is one of the few stallions who appears to do it very successfully. As well as working well with the Shamardal line he has also inbred very successfully back to both Danehill and Sadler's Wells. He tends to produce horses with quality which I thought might work here and although I don't think this is particularly relevant, GOLDEN GUEPARD from this family is by HURRICANE RUN from the same sireline.

TOO DARN HOT — I am putting him as a second option because I thought he might be a good physical fit for her and has a very good record with Shamardal mares [quite possibly because they compliment each other so well physically]. He is not in the top league and he is having a slightly quiet year but that is slightly forgivable given his current two and three-year olds are from his 3rd and 4th crops. In theory, we should be hearing a lot more from him as of next Autumn and he has managed to produce G1 winners from each of his first 3 crops including recent G1 winner GLACIUS whose second dam is also by Galileo. His record with Galileo mares is actually quite disappointing with only 2 SWs from 77 runners although one could make a case there are also 6 further Group placed horses among those.

KINGMAN — I am not sure if he will be predictable enough physically but he is a very good source of stakes winners which gives her a good chance of getting going. He is not quite at the top table, particularly when it comes to G1 winners but he is very versatile and produces stakes winners from 5 furlongs to middle distances and has worked well with both the Shamardal line to produce G1W FIELD OF GOLD as well as with her second dam sire Galileo to produce many SWs both on the direct and more generally including G1W COMMISSIONING.

mares.name: MELO MELO
mares.physical: As a top class racemare who was best over 2400m+ I would be aiming to breed a top class middle distance performer from MELO MELO. She needs a stallion who is proven to be effective with middle distance performers, albeit with a bit more precocity and speed than she had. She looks like a lovely big rangy mare with plenty of depth and lots of quality and a lot will depend on what her first foal is like.

plans2027.raceRecord: Unraced at two, a middle-distance / stayer, her minimum winning distance was 1m4f in May at three. She progressed to winning the Gr.2 Prix de Pomone on heavy before a close second to Warm Heart in the Gr.1 Prix Vermeille.
plans2027.pedigree: We’ve seen Gleneagles impart a lot of stamina and that looks the case here. She’s out of the 7f winner You Look So Good (Excellent Art), who is a full-sister to the Gr.2 Rockfel Stakes third Grey Pearl, and a half-sister to the 6f Gr.2 winner Electric Beat (Shinko Forest) in Germany and Listed-placed 2yo Blakey’s Boy (Hawk Wing). You Look So Good’s winning sister Lamyaa (Arcano) produced the Gr.1 Queen Elizabeth II Challenge Cup winner Lush Lips (Ten Sovereigns). Melo Melo is also a half-sister to the 5f Gr.3-winning juvenile who went on to win a Gr.3 over a mile at three, Treasuring (Havana Gold). Further back in the pedigree tells the same story - sprinter/milers, including the Irish Guineas third Cape Down by Green Desert’s Desert Style.
plans2027.analysis: She stayed well but her family is quicker, so she has lots of options. Any Classic sire should be ok. As we’ve touched on Justify and any Sadler’s Wells line mare, even allowing for the access he has to such quality, seems a positive. She ran plenty of times, which should help alleviate concerns about Justify’s occasional fragility, and even though she is 16.2hh, she has quality and balance. Justify is doing good stuff. Granted he has the support of the Coolmore broodmare band but to have won the three colts’ Classics already when his fourth crop are only three-year-olds this year is some accomplishment. He is excellent and a tough mare like this suits him. He has also had success with Immortal Verse (Pivotal) from three foals via Statuette. Gleneagles has no record yet as a damsire. She is really interesting with Justify given the speed and precocity in her pedigree, but her class over middle-distances. I also believe inbreeding to Storm Cat is a positive, even if only 5x4. It’s a genuine Derby/Oaks class pedigree. I put her on the ‘OK’ list for Night of Thunder. Everything about her is right for him bar the inbreeding to Galileo, which isn’t necessarily bad and has been done with success, it’s just worth noting. There are three foals of racing age on the cross. Dubawi has the progressive three-year-old Superior Choice with the Gosdens out of Gleneagles’s talented Gr.1-winning stayer Loving Dream, the only foal on the cross. He won the Listed Glasgow Stakes last time and looked to go wrong in the Voltigeur. Melo Melo won the same race Economics’ dam won and as a mare who stayed well, she ticks all boxes for the type of mare that suits him, it’s just whether you are happy with 3x3 to Galileo.

plans2027.title: MELO MELO 2019 by Gleneagles ex You Look So Good (Excellent Art)
plans2027.raceRecord: 7yo grey mare. 4 wins and 8 places from 15 starts including the G2 Prix de Pomone over 2500m in holding ground at 4. Beaten a short head in the G1 Prix Vermeille on good to soft ground the same year. She has a filly foal by Justify and is now in foal to Kingman.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the fourth foal of ten foals out of her winning dam YOU LOOK SO GOOD (Excellent Art). The first of these TREASURING (Havana Gold) won 4 races including two G3s - one at two over 5f and one at 3 over one mile. YOU LOOK SO GOOD has been well covered since but subsequent progeny have been disappointing. TREASURING has been covered by very good stallions in Japan so there is a chance of updates.

This is also the family of 2026 US 9f G1 winner LUSH LIPS (Ten Sovereigns) 6f G2 winner ELECTRIC BEAT [Shinko Forest] as well as multiple G1 winning miler PACO BOY (Desert Style). Aside from MELO MELO, the best horses in the family have had plenty of speed and been effective up to 9 furlongs. It is not obvious from her pedigree why she has so much stamina. That said, although Gleneagles’ progeny are effective over a range of distances he has a surprising amount of stakes winners at 2400m + (9).

Gleneagles is still relatively young as a broodmare sire with 4 crops to run for him. From 72 runners he has had 31winners including 2026 G1 Prix Jean Prat winner THESECRETADVERSARY [St Mark’s Basilica] and SW SUPERIOR CHOICE (Dubawi) as well as 2yo SP Stop The Nation [Sioux Nation]. It is not realistic to draw any conclusions from the above results but his sire Galileo is also an exceptional broodmare sire whose daughters have been effective with a wide range of stallions.

Second damsire Excellent Art had G1W CHANGINGOFTHEGUARD (by Galileo) in Australia this year as well as French G2 winner and G1 placed BRIGHT PICTURE (by Intello) both from the Galileo line.
plans2027.analysis:
LOPE DE VEGA — I think in spite of the negatives of the inbreeding, I am tempted to put this stallion as a first option. It feels like he could be a good physical match as she has lots of quality and he can bring power. He has now produced three G1 winners out of middle distance Galileo line mares. Although I know his sireline is less proven with the family and I still don't love his record with Mariah’ Storm on the dam side, 4 x 4 inbreedings don't tend to be particularly significant). He will be 20 next year which is still fine and the time could be great to use him as stallion statistics tend to drop after 20. She is in foal to Kingman and has a filly foal by Justify both of whom are much younger and she can go back to them if their stock is nice.

KINGMAN — She is in foal to him already and can easily go again as all the reasons for going still apply - he is a top class stallion from the Green Desert line which is responsible for PACO BOY and TREASURING. He has also proved very effective with Galileo line mares including two G1 winners out of dams with middle distance pedigrees. plans2027.pedigree:
She is the 2nd of nine foals out of NIGHT CARNATION who won 5 races including the G3 Coral Charge Sprint over 5f and was second in the G1 Nearctic Stakes over 6f at Woodbine. Night Carnation is the only black type winner out of placed RIMBA and third dam RISTNA won the G2 Sun Chariot Stakes in 1991. Further back this is also the family of G1Ws AMEERAT and COLLIER HILL.

Ocala is by NATHANIEL who has made a solid start as a broodmare sire with 10 stakes winners from 238 runners [4 %] and 7 Group winners including G1 winners TRIBALIST (Farhh) and ZELLIE (Wootton Bassett). His daughters have also had 2 individual SWs including G2W SILVER KNOTT from just three runners by Lope De Vega. Second dam sire SLEEPING INDIAN’s best as BMS is 5f G2W CATURRA by Mehmas and interestingly he has also produced G3 paced 2yo Tales Of The Heart by Mehmas from just four runners on that cross.

As her dam was also a sprinter, I think I would stick to a stallion with speed but proven to work with bloodlines with more stamina. Her Starspangledbanner cover looks good but he will be 21 next year and his fertility has always been difficult.

I feel like you can take a bit more of a chance with her as she has had 5 covers already and a lot will depend on what her progeny are like. He has also had three Group winners from 21 runners with Indian Ridge on the dam side (sire of second dam sire Sleeping Indian) including G1 winner KIND OF BLUE. Like him, his progeny look like they can be precocious, tough and train on. They appear to stay up to a mile but not much beyond.

plans2027.analysis: Zoustar is unproven as yet in this role, with just four SWs, one is by Justify, a Listed-winning Australian-bred colt. It’s a fast family, which should suit Justify, who has clicked with fast mares. He has a SW on the cross from four foals and he has done well in both hemispheres. The only reason he didn’t go back to Australia was because Coolmore thought he was too valuable. They shipped mares from Australia to him in the US to be covered So Hem time. He’s probably the one for her all things considered given her ability, pedigree and value. I like the fact he has worked well and is proven down there, it gives confidence to use him for a valuable mare like her. I had also mentioned Too Darn Hot for her last year but that can stay on the back burner unless you want to race it and breed to So Hem time in Australia. He accomplished the rare feat of Champion First and Second Crop sire down there, the first since Danehill to do it. She is in foal to Frankel presumably because they were both extremely classy racehorses. If the foal is nice, I would see no reason not to go back there if you are not keen on Justify for her. The pedigree doesn’t really point in any obvious direction for her up here.

plans2027.title: OLENTIA 2019 by Zoustar ex Mabkhara (Anabaa)
plans2027.raceRecord: 7yo mare and the winner of 7 races from 23 starts in Australia. She won her first two races at three over 1200 m and went on to win a G2 over 1500 m as well as two G3s over 1200 m and 1400 m. She is placed multiple times at Group level and her last race was a third place in the G1 Tatts Tiara over 1400m in June last year. She is in foal to Frankel for the first time.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is a half sister to multiple GW WANDABAA (Wandjina) and multiple SW and Group placed MALKOVICH (Choisir) as well as Group placed Seewhatshebrings (Sebring). There has been a nice black type update under the first dam this year as one of Olentia’s unraced sisters is the dam of Hong Kong G3 winner LITTLE PARADISE (by Toronado). Further back, this is also the family of Australian G1Ws REWAAYA and SENSE OF OCCASION.

Zoustar is still young as BMS with 4 SWs from 116 runners in 6 crops. I am reluctant to draw any conclusions from the figures as the numbers are still small and the bloodlines are different to European ones or behave differently. That said, he is the broodmare sire of G1 Blue Diamond Stakes winner and G1 Golden Slipper Stakes runner STREISAND (by Magnus from the Danehill line). In fact three out of four of his SWs as BMS are by stallions with Danehill blood. As a stallion, he has also produced 47 stakes winners including 7G1 winners with Danehill on the damside. Also worth noting is that one of his SWs is by JUSTIFY (his only runner on that cross)
plans2027.analysis:
NIGHT OF THUNDER — She is a very exciting mare being a G2 winner and a sister to three further black type horses. He is now in the elite league of stallions and as we have often said, incredibly versatile from an aptitude and bloodlines point of view. Unsurprisingly, he is pretty much unproven with these bloodlines though he has had 2026 SW OVERNIGHT out of an Anabaa mare as well as SW NIGHT TORNADO and two further Group placed horses from 12 runners with Anabaa on the dam side (some of it pretty tenous and I don’t think gives a clue either way). Even without a specific nick, he is a top class stallion that gives her every chance of producing a top class horse. If you prefer to wait to see what her Frankel looks like before going again, this would be a very good option.

FRANKEL — I had imagined she might be too big and plain for Frankel but if It works physically, the cross has been reinforced by the fact Zoustar appears to inbreed well back to Danehill both as a sire and a broodmare sire, including this year's G1 Blue Diamond Stakes Winner STREISAND.

There have been 29 runners with both Frankel and Redoute’s Choice blood and four Group winners including G2 winner MISS FABULASS. Interestingly, his son CRACKSMAN has produced G1W ACE IMPACT with Anabaa on the dam side and he himself has also produced G2 winner FRANCESCO GUARDI with Anabaa on the dam side. I would be pretty wary of drawing too many conclusions from that though and be more tempted by the fact that it is breeding the best to the best rather than any nick.

JUSTIFY — I have put him down as an option as he is the only one who is technically proven with her bloodlines -though that is more than likely to be just opportunity with JUSTIFY being dual hemisphere and could be very misleading. Interestingly though, he has had success with these lines, including Danehill but not yet with the Invincible Spirit line via I Am Invincible from 7 runners..
