mares.name: ONE LOOK
mares.physical: As a dual Group winner and G1 placed with a good pedigree with a lot of depth, she is a really exciting broodmare prospect. Physically, it sounds like she is reasonably straightforward and a nice type but could do with a stallion with a bit of leg.

plans2027.raceRecord: Won the 7f Goffs Million on her debut by six lengths, her only start at two. She won her 3yo debut over 7f on heavy ground and, at the third attempt and four starts later, won a Listed over a mile in August and was second in the 9.5f Gr.3 Denny Cordell, all at three. She was largely consistent in seven starts at four, all in Group company, winning a pair of Gr.3s from 8f-10f and placing twice in Gr.2s and beaten just a quarter of a length when third in the Gr.1 Prix de l’Opera. She didn’t appear to stay 12f in the Fillies and Mares behind Kalpana. She hasn’t won yet this season but is still performing with credit, best effort of three when second in the Gr.1 Pretty Polly Stakes.
plans2027.pedigree: Her dam Holy Salt (Holy Roman Emperor) placed at two and won over a mile at three. Her half-brother Baptism (Sea The Stars) was typical of his sire. He won a maiden at two, was a 10f Listed winner at three and won a 12f Gr.2 at four (in Italy). Progressive sort. Holy Salt is also a half-sister to an Australian 8f Gr.1 winner by Cape Cross, who won a 12f Listed in France as well, the 10.5f Gr.3 winner and Gr.1-placed Perfect Hedge (Unfuwain; dam of the smart stayer Called To The Bar by Henrythenavigator), another Listed-placed miler by Cape Cross and the useful Defrost My Heart, who has produced a Listed-placed Australia and Too Darn Hot. There are two more Listed-placed performers out of her second dam Via Saleria (Arazi) by Generous and Nayef. Via Saleria is a half-sister to the Gr.1-winning 2yo Poliglote (Sadler’s Wells).
plans2027.analysis: Northern Dancer seems to like this family. She is by Gleneagles, but her half-brother and her dam’s half-brother are by Sea The Stars and Cape Cross respectively and they are the best in the immediate family bar her. She is much better than her dam ever was and Holy Salt managed to produce a good horse by Sea The Stars. The foal would be inbred 2x4 to Urban Sea, which is no bad thing, and would have a Derby/Oaks class pedigree. One Look had precocity, though note that Sea The Stars Stakes-winning juveniles that go on are very rare, statistically if you don’t give them the time they need they will not fulfil their potential - The Lion In Winter is the latest victim of this and I hope Alpha is not the next. I conducted a study on this last year and there were just two Group-winning juveniles who won another Stakes as a three-year-old or older. So we don’t need a horse with juvenile form for Sea The Stars but it does no harm to send something that could show what One Look showed at two. He also fits the bill physically. Justify is the alternative selection. There is nothing in her family to point to his line really, though he is Northern Dancer albeit many generations away, but she is tough, she has run plenty of times and she is 8f-10f, which is the right profile for him. She’s also by a son of Galileo, who we know has lived up to expectation when paired with Justify. Justify is also known for putting size into his foals, something mentioned for her. Going the other way distance-wise but sticking with Green Desert’s sire line, Kingman also works for her on pedigree. The foal would be unlikely to stay beyond 1m2f, but for similar reasons to Sea The Stars, the sire line has worked well with her family and he can similarly help her out with leg. Kingman and Galileo mares have 11 SWs from 133 foals, which is just 8% and is fine. Kingman actually operates at 9% SWs to foals hence he is coming in third but could be an option for her in the future. Gleneagles is unproven as a damsire, he just has Thesecretadversary (St Mark’s Basilica) and one other SW at this stage. I like Sea The Stars as he has worked with the family and it brings in inbreeding to one of the best mares the breed has seen, but appreciate he had his issues last year, she is a talented maiden and now might be the best time to send her to Justify for her first cover. That said, there may not be many more chances (if any) to use Sea The Stars.

plans2027.raceRecord: 5yo racemare and the winner of 5 races from 17 starts from 7f to 10f including one at two and two G3s. She won the Goffs Million first time out in memorably impressive fashion. She won two races from six starts at three including a Listed race over a mile, and won two G3s at four, also finishing placed in the G1 Pretty Polly and Prix de l’Opera.
plans2027.pedigree:
ONE LOOK is the fourth of six foals out of the winning mare HOLY SALT whose second foal BAPTISM is a G3 winner over 12 furlongs in Italy as well as multiple Group placed. Holy Salt is a sister to Australian G1 winner HE’S YOUR MAN (Cape Cross) and French G3 winner PERFECT HEDGE (Unfuwain) who went on to produce three stakes horses including G2 winning stayer CALLED TO THE BAR (Henrythenavigator). There are also a number of black type horses under the second dam over both codes and the third dam is G3 winner ALEXANDRIE who is responsible for numerous G1 horses including POLIGLOTE (Sadler’s Wells) and SPECIAL RING (Nureyev).

Gleneagles is still relatively young as a broodmare sire with 4 crops crops to run for him. From 72 runners he has had 31winners including 2026 G1 Prix Jean Prat winner THESECRETADVERSARY [St Mark’s Basilica] and SW SUPERIOR CHOICE (Dubawi) as well as 2yo SP Stop The Nation [Sioux Nation]. It is not realistic to draw any conclusions from the above results but his sire Galileo is also an exceptional broodmare sire whose daughters have been effective with a wide range of stallions.

Holy Roman Emperor as BMS has worked particularly well with the Galileo line with 5 SWs including G1Ws JOHANNESS VERMEER and SHALE but interestingly he has also worked well with both the Scat Daddy line to produce PORTA FORTUNA (Caravaggio) and BRAVE EMPEROR (Sioux Nation) as well as two SWs by NO NAY NEVER. He has also produced G1Ws NEWSPAPEROFRECORD by Lope De Vega and CABALLO DEL MAR by his son Phoenix Of Spain as well as G3W and G1P RAYEKA by another son of Shamardal BLUE POINT.
plans2027.analysis:
JUSTIFY — It sounds like he would be good physically as well as on paper. Although he has not been tried with either Gleneagles or Holy Roman Emperor mares, he is known to be very effective with the Galileo line including G1Ws CITY OF TROY and SCANDINAVIA. He also has a very good strike rate with the Danehill line more generally with 15 stakes winners including G1 winners OPERA SINGER, SPICY MARTINI and ASPEN GROVE who all have Danehill on the dam side. He is from the Scat Daddy sireline which has worked well with Holy Roman Emperor mares to include G1 winner PORTA FORTUNA [by Caravaggio] and G2W BRAVE EMPEROR [Sioux Nation].

His progeny are also effective over a range of distances and although she won over 7 furlongs at two she was really a 10 furlong filly from a family with many middle distance horses. I think it will suit her well to go to a stallion with the range he has.

NOT THIS TIME — He is much less proven with her bloodlines but appears to be very versatile and is another who will suit physically. Although his record with his Galileo mares is nothing to write home about yet, he is from the same Giant’s Causeway sireline which has worked well with Holy Roman Emperor mares to produce 6 SWs including G1Ws CABALLO DE MAR and NEWSPAPEROFRECORD. I'm not convinced she needs a stallion with as much speed as this as she was best from a mile to furlongs and is from a family whose best horses have been over middle distances.

There is a 3 by 4 inbreeding to both Storm Cat and Mariah’s Storm but interestingly, he has been very effective with both - 21 stakes winners from 159 runners with Storm Cat on the dam side which is on a par with his normal statistics and 1 GW from 8 runners with Mariah’s Storm on the dam side.

LOPE DE VEGA — This is very much a third option in case you wanted to stay in Europe. As discussed, he works very well with both the Galileo and Danehill lines and is a super proven option who will not be around forever so this could be a good opportunity to use him.

plans2027.pedigree: This is a lovely middle-distance family. The dam Traffic Jam (Duke of Marmalade) didn’t make her debut until August at three over 12f in France. She won and also won a 1m7f from three starts at that age. She made six starts at four, placing in a 10f Listed, 12f Listed, 12.5f Gr.2, finished fourth in a competitive Prix Vermeille and won the 12f Gr.2 Prix du Conseil de Paris on her final start. She stayed well and progressed throughout her career. Her first foal Place Du Carrousel (Lope de Vega) was second on her only start at two in November and won her first two starts at three, including the Gr.3 Prix Cleopatre, before finishing second to Above The Curve in the Prix Saint-Alary when it was a Gr.1. She enacted revenge over Above The Curve and the Diane winner Nashwa in the Prix de l’Opera. She added another pair of Group contests at four from 8f-10f and moved to Australia for her five year old season, where she didn’t take to it (sold for €4m to Yulong at Arqana). The 3yo full-sister Place De l’Opera is with Andre and Lavinia Fabre and has finished mid-div in two starts to date this season. Traffic Jam has been to Dubawi and Kingman and had two fillies that never ran. Her sister by Fastnet Rock bred a Stakes-placed NZ-bred by Showcasing. Winged Cupid (In The Wings) was useful and is out of the third dam, a Shirley Heights half-sister to the dam of Lillie Langtry: Minding et al.
plans2027.analysis: Lope de Vega is the obvious starting point. She is a half-sister to a Gr.1 winner by him. It’s a decent cross from 46 foals, there are four SWs for 9%, that’s a point above Lope’s own SWs to foals percentage of 8%. They are the Gr.2 winner Beauvatier and three Listed winners. Sea The Stars is looking potentially top class as a damsire. That said, she has options because of Sea The Stars. He works brilliantly with Dubawi, though she has a half-sister that has disappointed by him. She would suit Night of Thunder but as he has limited access, there are better ones for him. Frankel has had three Stakes winners out of Sea The Stars mares (8%), including the classy Mohaafeth, and throughout her page Sadler’s Wells line sires have worked, most notably with Lillie Langtry. A Frankel foal would be inbred 3x3 Urban Sea, but also 3x4 Sadler’s and Danehill so there is a lot going on there. Physically, I think he would suit but as much as Lope and Dubawi to be fair. I wouldn’t be going to Justify with her as I think she stays a bit far and needs help in the speed/precocity department. She’s a useful but well-bred winner and I feel Lope is probably more her level and a good starting point. He can get a decent 2yo that will progress, so he should help her out there, we know he works with her family and he’s the right level to start her off.

plans2027.raceRecord: 4yo filly and the winner of one race over twelve furlongs from four starts in total, all at three.
plans2027.pedigree:
She was placed twice before winning by 5 lengths on her third start. She was then fried in Listed company where she finished 8th and has not run since. She was rated 97.

PEARLA is the 4th of 8 foals out of G2W TRAFFIC JAM [Duke Of Marmalade] who is the dam of G1 winner and multiple Group winner PLACE DU CARROUSEL (by Lope De Vega) and who has been back to Lope De Vega ever since. TRAFFIC JAM is the only stakes winner under her dam and stakes placed third dam Sweet Emotion produced SW and G1 Racing Post Trophy runner WINGED CUPID who was her only black type horse. The next dam HIWAAYATI is responsible for numerous G1 winners including LILLIE LANGTRY (Danehill Dancer), MINDING (Galileo), EMPRESS JOSEPHINE (Galileo) and TUESDAY (Galileo), and HENRY LONGFELLOW (Dubawi)

Sea The Stars is an excellent broodmare sire with 7% SW/Rs from 10 crops and 9 SWs including 12 G1Ws and 2026 Derby winner CHRISTMAS DAY (by Camelot). His daughters have a very good strike rate with Dubawi with 5 individual SWs from 16 runners (31%) including G1Ws ELDAR ELDAROV and AL HUSN. They also now have 4 individual SWs from 22 runners by his son NIGHT OF THUNDER including 2026 G3W AMBERGLEN. In spite of the inbreeding, the Kingman/Sea The Stars cross goes from strength to strength with 6 individual SWs and a really great 24% strike rate. He has also produced two G1 winners by Frankel [ONESTO and EL CORDOBES] albeit with a lower strike rate of 13% SW/R. He appears to be very versatile as a broodmare sire with stakes winners by 35 different stallions ranging from Mehmas to Le Havre.
plans2027.analysis:
LOPE DE VEGA — To me, she is a good one for this stallion for lots of reasons Including the fact that he will be a good fit physically. Not only has the direct cross worked well already, as well as more generally with Cape Cross, he has also worked very well with her second damsire Duke Of Marmalade, including producing her G1 winning half sister PLACE DU CARROUSEL.

JUSTIFY — If you wanted to cover her more ambitiously but avoid inbreedings, maybe JUSTIFY could be an option? He is a big horse but might suit for a first cover. The cross is unproven really but he has worked more loosely with both Cape Cross and Danehill so it is hard to imagine it would not work. I think I would prefer him to either FRANKEL or NIGHT OF THUNDER for her as with the inbreedings I feel there are probably better mares for them.

mares.name: REMARQUEE
mares.physical: She is very straightforward physically and her first foal sounds like a nice horse (bar turning in) from the original report.

plans2027.raceRecord: Won her only start at two in September over 7f. Won Gr.3 Fred Darling on soft, unplaced in 1000 Gs but good second in Coronation and Falmouth Stakes. Ran once at four in Gr.3 Chartwell and was fifth and retired. 7f/miler, any ground, backend two-year-old.
plans2027.pedigree: Kingman is just getting going now as a damsire. He has 394 foals of racing age and 8 SWs. Her pedigree hasn’t really moved since last year, Regardez’s first live foal since Revoir is a yearling colt by Kingman. Remarquee is out of the 1m2f Listed Hoppings Stakes winner Regardez (Champs Elysees) and a half-sister to the multiple Stakes-placed Revoir (Study Of Man), who operates between 10f and 12f. Regardez is a half-sister to the Gr.1 Prix Royal Oak winner Scope (Teofilo), and the Listed Prix Etoile winner Glance (Dansili). This appears to be a family that throws to the stallion and brings the class, hence Remarquee’s speed for a mile and her half-sister by Study Of Man getting further. She’s in foal to Night of Thunder, which gets more exciting with every passing week. Unless you want to repeat the dose, Frankel was my first suggestion last year and I still think he looks perfect for her. You’ll get a Guineas-class pedigree with 1m2f well within its remit, as well as enough in the mating to try 12f. There are lots of Juddmonte influences in Remarquee’s pedigree - Rainbow Quest, Champs Elysees, Kingman - which encourage going back to the farm that produced him. There is a Gr.1 winner by a son of Galileo on the page. She’s typical of her sire and Frankel imparts strength and substance, they should complement each other. At this stage, there is just the Listed winner and Group-placed Sand Gazelle on the cross from 15 foals. She’s bred similarly in that she is out of a 7f winner and from a top middle-distance family, though Remarquee had considerably more ability than Sand Gazelle’s dam. Night of Thunder was the second suggestion last year and that still works and I am excited to see the foal. She’s bred to want further than a mile and had more than enough talent to warrant a cover like him and if you like the foal then I see no reason not to go back there. As an alternative, she has a suitable profile for Justify, being from an excellent middle-distance family but have enough speed and shown form at two. She is also a typical Kingman and will benefit from a horse with Justify’s size and substance. The cross is untried, as is this sire line with this family. Frankel does edge it with a Gr.1 winner by Teofilo in her immediate family.

plans2027.title: REMARQUEE 2020 by Kingman ex Regardez (Champs Elysees)
plans2027.raceRecord: 5yo bay mare and a G3 winner over 7 furlongs and runner up in both the G1 Coronation Stakes and G1 Falmouth Stakes over a mile. Her first foal is a FRANKEL colt born in February who had screws put in three out of four of his ankles but other than that was a nice strong foal with the makings of a very nice horse (April report). She is in now in foal to NIGHT OF THUNDER.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the fourth of seven foals out of stakes winner and multiple Group placed REGARDEZ (Champs Elysees) who is also the dam of multiple stakes placed Revoir (Study Of Man) and has a Kingman yearling colt. This is also the family of G1 Oaks winner LOOK HERE (Hernando) as well as G1 winning stayer SCOPE (Teofilo)

Kingman made a steady start as BMS but he has had a couple of better stakes horses this year and last year and has now had 8 stakes winners from 206 runners (3%) from 5 crops of runners. Two of his stakes horses this year are 2yo G3 MOONRISE (Churchill) and Italian 2yo SW MAURIZIO ACQUAVIVA (Arizona), and his eight stakes winners and 11 stakes horses in total are all by different stallions.
plans2027.analysis:
FRANKEL — I think her stallion choice will depend largely on how much you like her first foal. The direct cross has only produced 1 stakes winner from 9 runners but that can change quickly from such small numbers. As with Julica, although his overall statistics when inbreeding back to Danehill are inferior, he has an excellent strike rate with Champ Elysees’ full brother Dansili. He now has 14 SWs from 95 runners with Dansili on the dam side including G1W MINNIE HAUK and SOUL SISTER as well as 2026 Group winners ITEM and GILDED PRIZE (though none yet with Champs Elysees from 4 runners).

NIGHT OF THUNDER — I'm a bit torn on this one as she is in foal to him already and on the one hand the direct cross has not produced a SW from 8 runners, yet he has produced multiple G1 winner BOW ECHO out of an Invincible Spirit mare as well as two further stakes winners and the numbers are probably not enough to be a negative. Added to that, if her first foal lacked a bit of leg and did not have perfect conformation, NIGHT OF THUNDER might not be the ideal stallion. That said, she is a very exciting young mare who has produced a very good first foal so from that point of view is an obvious one to put to him.

NOT THIS TIME — If you are not sure about her FRANKEL foal and would prefer to wait and see what her NIGHT OF THUNDER is like, NOT THIS TIME is a tall horse. Although he won on dirt, his sire GIANT’S CAUSEWAY was a top class European 10 furlong horse and he appears to be working with European bloodlines including the Invincible Spirit line.

mares.name: SCENIC
mares.physical: She is a really exciting young mare but she is small and needs a stallion with size and leg. Her options are also limited by the fact she already has Galileo on the dam side through Frankel. This is a family which has worked particularly well with the Dubawi and Galileo lines but with Frankel as a second damsire, there are no viable options without inbreeding, so she will have to go to a less proven cross.

plans2027.raceRecord: A very progressive type, she placed in a novice over 1m at two, contested Listed company and placed in her first four starts at three. Still a maiden, she placed twice in novice company, all 1m2f-1m4f. She shed her maiden in a 1m4f AW novice at four, was Listed-placed over 1m7f and won the 1m4f Galtres before finishing fourth in the Park Hill. She was at her best last year, second in a 1m4f Listed, winning the 1m6f Gr.3 Bronte Cup, and second to Estrange in the 1m4f Lancashire Oaks.
plans2027.pedigree: One of the best families in the studbook, which has only improved again with Diamond Necklace. Prudenzia et al are the gifts that keep on giving, and they are all given every chance.
plans2027.analysis: She is in foal to Justify which incorporates inbreeding to Storm Cat and suited her well. Both Dubawi and Night of Thunder have worked with this family before though not necessarily with Lope de Vega, both have just one SW each out of Lope mares: Night of Thunder has 1 SW from 10 foals, the Listed Galtres Stakes and Gr.2 Premio Lydia Tesio winner Charlotte’s Web. He is 10% SWs to foals and Lope mares aren’t quite doing it yet, so it is performing as it should. It’s also worth noting that Scenic is out of a Frankel mare and he has worked well with Dubawi mares and it’s just that Galileo/Dubawi mix that we know complements each other so well. Persica is a son of New Bay out of a Lope mare. Lope de Vega mares with Dubawi have 1 SW from only 9 foals - 11%, that’s fine. The SW is the Listed winner and Gr.2-placed Audubon Park, who was very talented but suffered a serious injury before the French Oaks. She is also from a similarly deep middle-distance family (Wertheimer’s Balladeuse/Left Hand etc). In her family, there is the Gr.2 Debutante winner and French Guineas third Vespertilio (Night of Thunder) and the Gr.3 winner Philomene and Gr.2 winner Emily Dickinson, both by Dubawi, all in the phenomenal Platonic branch. She is worth asking the question about Dubawi, if there is a possibility he is still going well, because we know he works phenomenally well with middle-distance mares. So does Night of Thunder, a foal by him would be 3x4 Galileo (thus 4x5 Urban Sea). Dubawi and Night of Thunder still top the list.

plans2027.title: SCENIC 2020 by Lope De Vega ex Ghalyah (Frankel)
plans2027.raceRecord: Late maturing/progressive 6yo mare and the winner of three races at 4 and 5 years including the G3 Bronte Cup over 1m6f last year. She also finished a close second in the G2 Lancashire Oaks over 1m4f last year. She is now in foal for the first time to Justify.
plans2027.pedigree:
SCENIC is the second of five foals foal out of the unraced Ghalyah (Frankel) who cost €1,150,000 as a yearling and is out of the blue hen mare Platonic whose offspring are highly sought after, having made a huge impact on the track and in the ring and include G1Ws CHICQUITA, MAGIC WAND and this year DIAMOND NECKLACE, as well as G1 placed EMILY DICKINSON, VESPERTILIO and PHILOMENE. Further back this is also the family of G1Ws MAGICAL ROMANCE, ALEXANDROVA, ASPETAR, CHANNEL and REKINDLING. At the moment Scenic is the only black type filly out of Ghalyah with no apparent yearling or foal.

Lope de Vega is a very good broodmare sire with 31 SWs from 619 runners (5%) in 9 crops. The best of these are 2026 G1 winners BENVENUTO CELLINI and ITEM (both by Frankel) – a cross which has produced 3 SWs in total from just 6 runners to date also including Benvenuto Cellini’s sister SW GISELLE. He also has two stakes winners apiece by Siyouni (25%) and New Bay (11%), But other than that his 31 stakes winners are all by different stallions ranging from middle distance stallions such as Camelot and Nathaniel to Sprint sires such as Kodiac and Mehmas.
plans2027.analysis:
JUSTIFY — He is still unproven with Lope De Vega mares but he is very much establishing himself as an elite stallion, particularly on the turf and in Europe. To me, he is still the best choice for her, slightly due to a lack of other good options for her which will also work physically.

He has produced 3 SWs from 29 runners with Giant’s Causeway on the dam side including dual turf G2W BUCHU who is bred similarly to SCENIC as she is out of a Galileo mare, with Giant’s Causeway as second dam sire. He has worked very well with the Galileo line with 10 SWs including G1Ws CITY OF TROY and SCANDINAVIA.

CAMELOT — He is not as versatile as JUSTIFY, but if you are not afraid of breeding a slow maturing middle distance horse [particularly out of this mare] CAMELOT has a very good affinity with Lope De Vega and his sire Shamardal, as well as inbreeding successfully back to Sadler’s Wells and in particular the Galileo line. There have been 3 runners by Camelot under Platonic, one of which is stakes winner ENGLISH KING and G1W CHIQUITA and G3W PACIFIQUE are by his sire MONTJEU. Although he is not a big horse, he stamps his stock and they tend to be very good looking, well balanced horses, not lacking in size.

plans2027.raceRecord: Quite versatile, she has performed well from 6.5f-1m, on turf, AW and dirt, and soft and fast ground. Probably best 7f-8f. Pretty early, she was third on debut in June at two. Perhaps something went amiss as she didn’t run again until September, when second in a 7f maiden before winning a 7f conditions race comfortably at Newbury the same month. An AW handicap off 87 was her best effort at three. Switching to the US, she won a pair of allowances over 8f-8.5f on turf and dirt but found Graded Stakes too tough. A useful sprinter miler.
plans2027.pedigree: She is one of five winners out of the Listed winner Pacific Angel (Dalakhani), herself the best of six winners out of the Sadler’s Wells mare Pestrovka, a full-sister to the 12f Gr.2 winner Policy Maker, half-sister to the Gr.2 stayer Pushkin (Caerleon) and Gr.3 Lancashire Oaks winner Place Rouge, as well as the dam of Planteur and grandam of Persian King. Serene Seraph’s brother Blarney (Belardo) has won a Listed over 1m7f this year. It’s a renowned Wildenstein family, that of Peinture Celebre et Al, and a typical middle-distance one for the outfit. Pacific Angel has had good opportunities, the Frankel is a handicapper and her Belardo and Serene Seraph are her best to date, both by Shamardal descendants. Dalakhani is a good damsire, Blue Point will take a while to get a record. I expect her dam’s stamina influences, she’s out of a mare by Sadler’s Wells, have definitely had a say and should be kept in mind.
plans2027.analysis: Given her pedigree, I am treating her as a miler rather than a sprinter and believe she could well produce mile plus offspring. She is in foal to Justify, which appealed on pedigree, ability and Storm Cat inbreeding, though distant (5x5). However, back in Europe, Sadler’s Wells has worked very well with the family so Frankel comes into the reckoning, he is the best available from the Sadler’s line. Frankel and Shamardal mares are an ok cross (4 SWs for 11% SWs to foals, just shy of Frankel’s 12% SWs). That said, her half-brother by Frankel was moderate but as John Magnier always liked to point out, City Of Troy’s year older brother had nothing on him! I would argue he was still above average though (rated 104 here and won the London Gold Cup before export!). Given she stayed a mile and she has some lovely classy middle-distance types in her family, one sire who does work particularly well with Shamardal is Sea The Stars. He has 6 SWs from 52 foals for 12%, including the Gr.1 winner Sosie, Gr.2 winner Silver Lady, multiple Gr.3 winner Al Aasy and three Listed winners. Cape Cross also has two SWs, including the Classic winner Awtaad from just two foals. She was on the list of ok suitables for Night of Thunder because she does suit him but there are others who suit him more. She is quite a fun mare to mate because she was versatile herself and has that classic distance pedigree behind her. I did look at Not This Time but the foal would be 2x4 Giant’s Causeway and that’s not something that I have seen to work. The top foals bred on the cross per my research are ordinary winners. If you want to keep her in the US then I wouldn’t let that stop you but she is probably better served by Sea The Stars or Frankel. Some middle-distance sire power paired with her blend of speed and stamina is appealing.

plans2027.title: SERENE SERAPH 2121 by Blue Point ex Pacific Angel (Dalakhani)

preferences.tag: 3 x 4 inbreeding to Sadler’s Wells 22 SWs and 5 G1Ws including PIERRE BONNARD

plans2027.raceRecord: 5yo filly and the winner of 4 races from 14 starts. She was placed twice in competitive maidens before winning easily over 7 furlongs third time out in September at two. She won one race (7f) from three stars at three in the UK before being transferred to the US where she won her first two starts over a mile but did not make the grade in stakes company after that. She is in foal for the first time to Justify.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the third of seven foals and one of four winners out of PACIFIC ANGEL who won a Listed race over 2000m at four. There has been a nice update this year as her 4yo brother BLARNEY by BELARDO won a Listed race in Italy over 1m7f. PACIFIC ANGEL is the only black type filly out of a winning full sister to multiple G2 winner POLICY MAKER (Sadler’s Wells) as well as G2W PUSHKIN (Caerleon), G3W PLACE ROUGE (Desert King) and a number of other black type horses. Another sister PLANTE RARE is responsible for G1W PLANTEUR (Danehill Dancer) as well as the dam of G1W PERSIAN KING (Kingman).

Although she had speed and was best at 7f to a mile (possibly because of Blue Point) this is a good French family which has generally been best at around 2000m.

Blue Point is too young to have any runners as BMS but his sire Shamardal is a very good broodmare sire with 7% SW/Rs and 154 SWs overall including 19 G1Ws. He has 7 SWs including G1W HELLO YOUMZAIN by KODIAC, 7 SWs including G1 winning siblings ALTHIQA and MYSTERIOUS NIGHT by DARK ANGEL and 7 SWs including G1W LATROBE by CAMELOT.
plans2027.analysis:
SEA THE STARS — Although she is by BLUE POINT who was a sprinter and I always feel Sea The Stars works best with more classic bloodlines, she was best over 7 to 8 furlongs and from a middle distance family. He has worked very well with Shamardal mares with 6 SWs from 34 runners including G1W SOSIE. More generally, he loves Darshaan and Sadler’s Wells which she has through PACIFIC ANGEL. He is a top class stallion who won’t be around forever and would give her a very good second cover.

KINGMAN — No cross will be proven as Blue Point is too young, but Kingman has worked with these various bloodlines and in particular Shamardal to produce G1W FIELD OF GOLD. He is also the sire G1W PERSIAN KING from this family (under the third dam). He is not in the same league as the best stallions but he still is a very good source of stakes winners and Group winners and a very good option with good reasons to use for her second cover.

CAMELOT — Although she is by Blue Point who was a sprinter, she was better over 7f to 8f, and is from a middle distance family. Camelot has worked well with these bloodlines and Shamardal in particular, and also inbreeds very well to Sadlers Wells [unlike most other stallions]. He is a very reliable source of middle distance class, which suits this family well. The only runner from this family by Camelot is stakes placed The Famous Five (albeit under the third dam).

mares.name: SHINE ON ME
mares.physical: She is a neat type, has substance and nice outlook. Typical of her sire. Best to go to something with size and leg.

plans2027.raceRecord: Ran only over 5f. Debut third in May as two, won at the seventh attempt, though took in Stakes in the intervening five starts, running with credit without winning. She was 6th in the Queen Mary, 4th in the Duchess of Cambridge, 2nd in Listed Prix de la Valle d’Auge on good to soft and 3rd in the Gr.3 Prix d’Arenberg. Ran once at 3 and disappointed. She was a 60,000gns yearling and purchased for £160,000 at Doncaster Breeze-Up Sale.
plans2027.pedigree: She is the first foal out of an unraced mare, her half-brother by Belardo (2yo) is in training with Archie Watson. The second dam Golden Nun (Bishop Of Cashel) was also precocious, ran at Royal Ascot at two but trained on, having been Listed-placed over 6f at two in Italy and won over 5f. She was Group-placed at three, all bar one of her 14 starts over 6f. She made 13 starts at four, culminating in the Gr.3 Ballyogan Stakes and Listed Kilvington Stakes, both 5f and on firm and good ground. Very sound and very tough, like her 138-raced 11-time winner Confessional (Dubawi), also a sprinter and Gr.3-placed.
plans2027.analysis: She was a precocious juvenile just below genuine Stakes class, OR96 at her best, and had lots of speed. I think we should take her as she is, but go with the sprinter/miler sire who has at least shown he can get a top-class miler. He has two now and that is Blue Point (Rosallion and Blue Bolt, though both had assistance from their dams). Blue Point has very quickly developed a strong affinity with Oasis Dream mares and sons, most recently Samangan landed the Maurice de Gheest and it was almost a double for the cross with Folsom Blues second in the Phoenix on the same day. There is also the Gr.1 winner Big Evs and Gr.2 winner Elmonjed. Shine On Me is by Havana Grey but out of a Fountain Of Youth (Oasis Dream) mare. I think this is the best way to breed to her pedigree and profile but have a chance of getting something with more scope. No Nay Never must also be considered as the undisputed king of two-year-olds. Though he did have True Love this year and has Alcohol Free, I would not expect anything like that from Shine On Me. You would be looking at breeding an Ascot two-year-old with no expectations of it training on but it would be a shock if it didn’t work! The fact she has a nice outlook is also a big advantage for No Nay. Never So Brave is out of an Oasis mare, one of 6 SWs from 31 foals and 19% SWs to foals on the cross. We also know that Scat Daddy and Galileo like each other, so the lines are all little positives.

plans2027.title: SHINE ON ME 2023 by Havana Grey ex Motsi Ma Boati (Fountain Of Youth)
plans2027.raceRecord: 3 year old filly who raced eight times in total including seven at two and all over five furlongs. She was third first time out in May as a 2yo and was then campaigned ambitiously, finishing 6th in the G2 Queen Mary at Royal Ascot. She finished second in a Listed race at Deauville in August and third in a G3 race Longchamp, also in August. She then won a novice race at Wolverhampton in October and had just the one start at three, finishing second last.
plans2027.pedigree:
Shine On Me is the first of four foals out of the unraced Motsi Ma Boati (Fountain Of Youth) who is the daughter of G3 and Listed winner GOLDEN NUN [Bishop of cashel] who was campaigned mostly over six furlongs and won five races from 42 runs in total. She was placed thirteen times including nine at stakes level. Her only black type horse is Confessional (Dubawi) who won 11 races and was placed forty times, including finishing second in the G3 Sprint stakes at Sandown. As you would expect for a filly from the 4th crop of Havana Grey, this is a family with plenty of speed and toughness but quite light on black type.

Havana Grey has only had one runner as BMS and his sire HAVANA GOLD has not yet had a stakes horse from 60 runners. I'm not sure I would let that bother me too much as neither is particularly typical of their respective sires. Havana Grey takes more from his broodmare sire Dark Angel.
plans2027.analysis:
BLUE POINT — I think I would be a bit cautious of trying to draw too many conclusions from the cross as the sires in her pedigree are either unproven or slightly obscure. You could easily make a case that Blue Point has already worked with the Galileo line to produce G1W ROSALLION and has worked particularly well with Oasis Dream (sire of Fountain Of Youth) line mares to produce 5 SWs including G1Ws BIG EVS and SAMANGAN but I don’t think her particular bloodlines are very representative of those stallions.

That said, she was a very fast filly and given he was a multiple Royal Ascot winner whose 2yos made such an impact you could really hope to breed a Royal Ascot 2 year old on this cross. The best horses in this family had lots of speed and I think I would be tempted to stick with that.

NOT THIS TIME — They were being very selective over his mares last year so I don't know If this is a realistic choice but he is a tall horse with lots of speed which I thought might suit. He is a top class sire of 2 year olds and up and would be fantastic just on that basis. As above, you could make a case that he has proved versatile enough to work with the Galileo line and has also worked with the Green Desert line to produce Royal Ascot G2 Norfolk Stakes winner SHAREHOLDER but I am recommending it more because he is suitable physically and from an aptitude point of view and a great outcross for her.

mares.name: SOPRANO
mares.physical: She looks fairly straightforward physically, though I made a note that she is offset.

plans2027.raceRecord: A very tough filly, made 18 starts, won 4 and placed 8 times. Had a wind op. Precocious filly, made a winning debut over 5f at two and Gr.3 Albany Stakes third amongst four Stakes-placed efforts over 6f/7f at two. Won Sandringham Handicap at Royal Ascot off OR100. Three-length Gr.3 Prix de Lieurey winner and twice Gr.1-placed at three. Won Listed Snowdrop over Crimson Advocate by a nose first time out at four, last twice after and retired. Sharp, early, quick, tough, sprinter/miler. Genuine Gr.3 class.
plans2027.pedigree: She is the first foal out of an unraced half-sister to the three-time US Gr.1 winner Obviously by SSB’s sire Choisir. They’re out of another unraced mare, this one a Montjeu half-sister to a Listed Hurdler. Pedigree-wise, she has that Sadler’s/Montjeu influence, which we have seen used to such good effect with her sire. Her dam has had just two foals and both have won at Royal Ascot after her 3yo Moonfall (Starman) won the Britannia Stakes. There is not much to go on for her elsewhere in the pedigree.
plans2027.analysis: She is in foal to Night of Thunder, which was a great cover to start her off. Frankel was my first suggestion for her last year ahead of him and nothing has changed to think otherwise, if anything, the further success of Starspangledbanner with Sadler’s Wells line mares has enhanced it. The lines really complement each other. Precise is the latest example. Starspangled is just getting started as a damsire, he has added two new SWs in this role, one by Night of Thunder (Lw Great Wish) and another, the Gr.1 Phoenix Stakes winner Sun Goddess (Sioux Nation). Without much of a record, it is good to take a lead from SSB’s own remarkable affinity with Sadler’s Wells line mares and the best of those around now is Frankel, who she more than warrants. You should get a two-year-old that progresses and easily gets a mile at three. I suggest Frankel and if the foal is gorgeous, go back to Night of Thunder the following year. There is a minor SW from the only foal on the cross and it makes sense to send a classy and tough miler like her to him.

plans2027.title: SOPRANO (2021) by Starspangledbanner ex Lealas Daughter (Excelebration)
plans2027.raceRecord: 5yo young mare and the winner of 4 races in 18 starts including the G3 Prix de Lieurey over a mile at three. She won first time out over 5f in May as a 2yo before finishing third in the G3 Albany Stakes at Ascot. She has been placed 8 times at stakes level and has run some excellent races in defeat including 2nd in the G1 Queen Elizabeth Challenge Cup Stakes over a mile at Keeneland and 3rd in the G1 Matron Stakes over a mile. She is in foal for the first time to Night Of Thunder.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the first foal and only black type filly to date out of the unraced Excelebration mare Leala’s Daughter, who is a sister to dual US G1 winner OBVIOUSLY (Choisir). He won 13 races in total from 6 ½ furlongs to a mile and was placed numerous times at Group level. They are the only two black type horses under the first three dams. Her three-year old brother MOONFALL (by Starman) won the Britannia and could easily go up in grade depending on where he goes. He is rated 97.

Starspangledbanner has had an amazing year as a sire as well as a broodmare sire. He is now the broodmare sire of G1 winning 2yo filly SUN GODDESS (by Sioux Nation) as well as recent G3W GREAT WISH (by Night Of Thunder). Added to that, he is also the broodmare sire of this year’s G2 Railway Stakes third Confucius (by No Nay Never). In total he has now had 3 SWs and 7 stakes placed horses from 167 starters (1.8%).

As her dam is by Excelebration, she is inbred 4 x 4 to Danehill.
plans2027.analysis:
JUSTIFY — Although it is not a proven cross he is by Scat Daddy, sire of Sioux Nation who is responsible for SUN GODDESS. One horse does not make a statistic but it's nice to know that cross has worked and Justify has also worked well with Danehill Dancer on the dam side to produce 3 SWs including G1W OPERA SINGER (second dam by Danehill Dancer) as well as the Danehill line more generally, albeit often in the second generation, which is good given that she has inbred to him.

LOPE DE VEGA — She is inbred to Danehill and he has worked really with mares from various branches of the Danehill line, including Danehill Dancer (6 SWs including G3W ECRIVAIN) and Exced And Excel (3 SWs including G3W SHOMARIA). He also has a very good strike rate with third damsire Montjeu (12 SWs including G1W AUNT PEARL). Although his results with those particular crosses are not his most spectacular, he is such a good source of Group and stakes winners who is proven with those lines and made his name with much lesser mares. Her pedigree is on the light side and I feel he would be a good fit on paper.

NIGHT OF THUNDER — Last year you were keen to send her to NIGHT OF THUNDER and she is in foal to him. I thought you might prefer to change the mares you send to him this year but this option is still a good one. She is inbred to Danehill through Starspangledbanner and Exceed And Excel and so far crosses with those stallions have not produced a G1 winner but have been effective at producing Group winners.

He has sired 7 SWs and 3 further stakes placed horses from 30 runners with Danehill Dancer on the dam side and 4 Stakes winners from 28 runners with Exceed And Excel on the dam side including three G3Ws. More broadly speaking, he has sired 39 SWs including G1Ws HIGHFIELD PRINCESS, OMBUDSMAN and PORTFOLIO DURATION from 277 runners with Danehill on the dam side. He has also produced 6 SWs including G2W AUYANTEPUI with Montjeu on the dam side.

mares.name: STAY ALERT
mares.physical: She looks a nice quality mare who could do with a correct stallion with lots of power/strength. On paper Justify is a very good mating for her so a lot will depend on how you like her first foal. If you really like it, all the same reasons still apply that the cross is proven with both Fastnet rock and Galileo and his two year old's from his fifth crop look very exciting. If having been twice you would like to look at something else here are a couple of options below:

plans2027.raceRecord: Unraced at two, off the mark over 1m4f on AW by April at three and a Listed winner over 1m2f by June. She was exceptionally consistent from 1m1f to 1m4f thereafter in Group company, probably unlucky not to strike at the top level.
plans2027.pedigree: She is by a very good damsire and out of a mare by the best of the modern era. It is no surprise that Galileo and Fastnet have such a good record together given Fastnet is by Danehill. She is bred on the reverse of that cross. Her dam was a progressive middle distance racemare, consistent and durable, made 20 starts and her full-sister Star Rock was similar. She is a half-sister to the dam of Sumo Sam, Seaduced (Lope de Vega), who never ran and also produced a Listed winner also by Fastnet Rock. Her grandam Farfala was a classy 1m4f filly too and produced the Listed Zetland winner and Gr.2-placed Under The Rainbow (Fantastic Light), dam of the Gr.3 winner Luncies (Iffraaj), and the Sea The Stars mare Sweeping Up, who was second in the Gr.3 Pinnacle and produced the useful Listed-placed Sweeping by Siyouni. It’s a pedigree to try and get a Derby/Oaks contender. Justify has a very good record of 6 SWs from 51 foals of racing age - 17% with Fastnet Rock mares (15 are 2yos) vs his overall 6% SWs to foals of racing age. Likewise, for Justify with Galileo mares, he has 10 SWs from 100 foals of racing age (10%) out of Galileo mares. Soundness and longevity appear to be the only chink in Justify’s armour to date, so a tough mare like this one from a tough family is right up his alley as he works with both of her influences. She did stay a little bit further than we’ve seen work to best effect with Justify but it’s only a matter of time before that works. She foaled on March 3rd and was barren from an April 18th cover. I’m assuming her foal is nice and if she is staying in America, I would not see a reason not to go back. I won’t suggest Night of Thunder again as there is the note about her conformation, though her pedigree and her own ability and stamina are what he works well with. If she stays in America and you want a change, I’ve looked into Not This Time for her. There is a foal bred on the cross and it’s the Gr.2-winning turf miler Giocoso. His dam won a handicap over 7f and is out of a Storm Cat mare from a fast family though. We don’t know what Not This Time would’ve done had he stayed sound but he did win over a mile at two and was bred to get further. He has shown he can get 5f sprinters and 12f+ Gr.1 horses and there is no reason to think she would not suit him. I have never seen him so I don’t know if he is correct but have never heard any warnings. He will only start to have any sort of record with European pedigrees over the next few years and we’ll learn more, but he is such a fantastic stallion and she is a classy mare, I see no reason why it shouldn’t work. If she comes back, a visit to Sea The Stars would produce a Derby-class pedigree and be inbred 2x4 to Urban Sea, which is a plus. She was more than a stayer as she showed class from 9f to 12f. STS and Fastnet have no SWs from 15 foals but that’s a small sample. Sea The Stars works best with mares similar to himself and he is ultra consistent with black-type mares, sending him a Stakes winner that operated in her range and with a pedigree like hers is exactly what works best with him.

plans2027.title: STAY ALERT 2019 by Fastnet Rock ex Starfala (Galileo)
plans2027.raceRecord: 7yo bay mare in foal for the second time to Justify. She won 4 races at 3 and 5 years and 3 stakes races including the G2 Dalhia Stakes (1m1f) and was second in the G1 Pretty Polly Stakes (1m2f).
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the last foal out of her G2 placed dam Starfala (Galileo). Her full sister STAR ROCK (2014) is a stakes winner and twice G2 placed but has not produced a stakes winner yet. This is a lovely late maturing middle distance family and her unraced sister Seaduced (Lope De Vega) is the dam of dual G2 winner SUMO SAM as well as 2026 Australian dual stakes winner SUN GOD (Fastnet Rock). Further back are also a number of middle distance stakes winners including G2 Lancashire Oaks placed UNDER THE RAINBOW (Fantastic Light), G3 placed FARFALA (Linamix) and G3 placed THUNDER ROLL (Night Of Thunder).

Fastnet Rock is a good broodmare sire with 150 SWs (5%) in 14 crops including 16 G1Ws. He has a very good strike rate with Galileo with 10 SWs from 37 runners (27%) including G1Ws WARM HEART and RUSSIAN EMPEROR. The nick is also very strong the other way round – 31 SWs from 166 runners including 11 G1Ws – hence STAY ALERT. But he also works very well with other stallions including Lope De Vega and Justify (albeit largely in Australia).
plans2027.analysis:
NOT THIS TIME — He could be very good US option for her as he has already shown he can work with Fastnet Rock mares and with Danehill more generally. Again, the numbers are too small to make a statistic but he is by GIANT'S CAUSEWAY and for a stallion who started off relatively cheaply in the US, he has shown that his progeny are already working on turf and with European bloodlines. Interestingly this mating produces 5 x 5 inbreeding to Crimson Saint and GIOCOSO has two strands of Crimson Saint in the 5th generation, while there are 7 of his offspring with Crimson Saint on the dam side including G1 winner JUST ONE TIME.

My one concern is that he is much more of an influence for speed and precocity which may not be a perfect fit for this family. If it works, it will inject a bit of both but it also may not bring out the best in her.

LOPE DE VEGA — He would be a very proven option with a well established affinity with Fastnet Rock mares (and Danehill more generally) as well as Galileo mares. She has lots of quality and looks like she would suit him physically. He is not quite in the same league as the very best stallions but would give her a very good chance of producing a Group horse and could be a good option for a third cover.

CAMELOT — Camelot is a bit of an anomaly, particularly for a stallion whose progeny can be quirky, in that many of his best bred horses are inbred back to either Danehill or Sadler’s Wells. This is a lovely middle distance family and I thought he might suit her well If you wanted to produce a Derby horse. Mind you, JUSTIFY would do just the same although I don't think LOPE DE VEGA would!

mares.name: SUMO SAM
mares.physical: She is a lovely staying mare to breed from but she is difficult as she is big and her first foal by Dubawi was big, so size is definitely a major consideration. Also, being inbred to Galileo and out of a Lope De Vega mare makes things complicated if trying to avoid further inbreeding. The stallions on the list which avoid further inbreeding and would be good on paper [JUSTIFY, NOT THIS TIME and KINGMAN] don't feel like a good fit physically. Even without having to factor in the sales ring aspect, it doesn't seem like a good idea to go to a big stallion.

plans2027.raceRecord: Won only start at two over 7f. Took time to find her feet at three (August), though she was highly tried. She was a surprise winner of the Gr.2 Lillie Langtry at Goodwood but backed it up in the Gr.2 Park Hill. She couldn’t recapture her form at four.
plans2027.pedigree: Out of an unraced Lope de Vega sister to Stay Alert and Star Rock. Under Farfala, there is the Gr.3 winner Luncies by Wootton Bassett’s sire Iffraaj. Pedigree as above, the family are generally speaking 8f-12f. There is a useful middle distance filly named Thunder Roll by Night of Thunder on the page but given she is already inbred to Galileo (3x4), I’m inclined to look towards Mr Prospector line sires rather than Galileo/Northern Dancer. It was concluded that she needed something with a bit of speed and so she went to Dubawi, who has a strong record with mares like her. She is in foal to Dubawi and Kingman was the second suggestion for her last year. To repeat myself, temperament is definitely important here, as Nathaniel fillies can be hot and Kingman can pass on some temperament too. He should suit her physically, as she has good bone and ran plenty of times. Kingman is almost completely free of Northern Dancer (5th generation via Green Desert), which we need to think about if she has a filly as she is already inbred 3x4 Galileo. Kingman has just 6 foals out of Nathaniel mares but we know he works fine with Galileo mares. She could benefit from his speed influence. A discussion was had about Zarak instead of Dubawi last year, which I like but don’t expect a 2yo as both needed time. Apart from that, it’s a lovely mating for her. With her inbreeding, her options are limited on these shores. She could also come into consideration for the two in America. Justify, as we know, works exceptionally well with Galileo and Sadler’s Wells, which she has a lot of. With her Lope blood, there is also a bit of Storm Cat on both sides. She stayed further than ideal based on what Justify has shown to date, though there are not many classy mares that stayed this far by nature of the programme book. She did win at two as well over 7f and it’s not a family of boats, they have class. I like him for her. Mares that suit Justify also suit Not This Time, by nature of the fact they are both high-class stallions, though the latter probably imparts that bit more speed. I haven’t seen Not This Time, so if you have strong feelings about what suits better physically then I would use that to decide. Pedigree-wise, they honestly both suit her really well and it’s something that warrants a discussion with a focus on the physicals rather than an essay from me. She had the 2yo form and she has the right pedigree and class to hope for a Classic horse from both.

plans2027.title: SUMO SAM 2020 by Nathaniel ex Seaduced (Lope De Vega)
plans2027.raceRecord: 6yo grey mare and a winner first time out over 7 furlongs at two before going on to win the G2 Lillie Langtry Stakes (14f) at Goodwood and the G2 Park Hill Stakes (14 ½ f) at Doncaster at three, both on soft ground and both from the front. She is in foal to Dubawi for the second time having produced a very good but big first foal by him.
plans2027.pedigree:
She is the 1st foal out of an unraced half sister to G2 winner and G1 Pretty Polly Stakes runner up STAY ALERT and stakes winner and twice G2 placed STAR ROCK. Her five year old brother SUN GOD (Fastnet Rock) has given the pedigree a nice update this year by winning two stakes races in Australia over 1300m and 1600m. Second dam is the G2 placed Starfala (Galileo). Seaduced has a Camelot 2yo filly, a Nathaniel yearling colt and a Study of Man filly foal.

This is a lovely late maturing middle distance family with a number of middle distance stakes winners including stakes winning second dam FARFALA (Linamix) who produced G2 Lancashire Oaks placed UNDER THE RAINBOW (Fantastic Light), and G3 placed THUNDER ROLL (Night Of Thunder).

Sumo Sam is by Nathaniel and inbred 2 x 3 to Galileo. Nathaniel has made a good start as a broodmare sire with 10 stakes winners from 238 runners [4%] and 7 Group winners including G1 winners TRIBALIST (Farhh) and ZELLIE (Wootton Bassett). This year he is the broodmare sire of G2 Ribblesdale Stakes winner EARTH SHOT. His daughters have also produced two individual stakes winners by Sumo Sam’s second damsire Lope De Vega but other than that all his stakes horses have been by different stallions from different lines.
plans2027.analysis:
BOW ECHO — I deliberated for a long time before suggesting him as he is unproven and has Galileo through NIGHT OF THUNDER. But she has been to Dubawi twice and I thought it might be better to go unproven than proven but unsuitable. He was a top class racehorse and a miler from a beautiful family. He himself is inbred to Zomaradah who was not only a G1W herself but also a great broodmare and the dam of Dubawi. It makes for a pretty interesting five generation pedigree! But on the other hand, he is a small horse with a fantastic turn of foot from a family and a sireline that is not all about speed and also proven to love Galileo, which I think could suit really well.

KINGMAN — As said above, I suspect it is high risk physically but on paper this is a good cross. He has proved very effective with Galileo line mares including two G1 winners out of dams with middle distance pedigrees. He has also produced 3 SWs including G1 winner FIELD OF GOLD out of Shamardal mares (sire of 2nd dam sire Lope De Vega) So it feels like a nice mix of bloodlines.
